Tech Report: Toulouse vs Rennes - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (539 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joel Lefevre | 27 Nov 2026 01:56.
  • Toulouse can potentially climb into the top half of the Ligue 1 table with a win over Rennes on Sunday at Stadium de Toulouse.
  • Both teams walked away with 1-1 draws the last time out, with Le Tefece sitting 12th after collecting a point versus Lens, putting them three points behind Rennes, who are ninth, after drawing Lorient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 27 Nov 2026 01:56.

Toulouse can potentially climb into the top half of the Ligue 1 table with a win over Rennes on Sunday at Stadium de Toulouse.

Both teams walked away with 1-1 draws the last time out, with Le Tefece sitting 12th after collecting a point versus Lens, putting them three points behind Rennes, who are ninth, after drawing Lorient.

For the second time domestically this season, Toulouse failed to emerge victorious last week when scoring first.

Those four points dropped represent the difference between their current position and a spot in Europe next season.

On the other hand, they have avoided defeat in seven of their last eight league games, including the last three at Stadium de Toulouse.

In their last three Ligue 1 home contests, this team have netted a combined six goals, six more than in their opening two games played in Toulouse.

Discipline has been an problem for Jens Berthel Askou’s men in the top flight this season, as they average the second-most fouls per match in the competition (15.7).

Toulouse can extend their Ligue 1 home unbeaten run versus Rennes on Sunday to five matches, last beating them in Toulouse in 2025 (2-1).

A campaign that began with so much promise has deteriorated for Stade Rennais, who have struggled to find consistency this month.

Franck Haise’s men are on a five-match winless run across all competitions, having begun 2026-27 unbeaten in their first five competitive fixtures.

A 3-1 loss at NEC in Europa League action on Thursday has them narrowly above the knockout stage line in that competition.

In November, they have netted a goal or fewer in each of their competitive games, while conceding a combined six times in their last three competitive outings.

Away from home, Rennes have really been exposed defensively in the league, conceding a combined 14 goals in their last four domestic matches as the visitors.

Les Rouge et Noirs are second in the league regarding expected goals, though they have conceded more penalties than anyone in the competition so far (five).

Rennes form (all competitions):.

Toulouse may be without Mark McKenzie, who suffered a hamstring strain in their last match, while Aron Donnum is eligible to return from his suspension.

Jacen Russell-Rowe netted for them in the opening half at Lens, his third of the Ligue 1 campaign, tied with Thomas Jorgensen for second on the team.

A minor knock has Valentin Rongier questionable in this outing for Rennes, while Adrien Thomasson will miss the match with a red-card suspension.

Boulaye Dia scored in their draw at arch-rivals Lorient last Sunday, putting him up to six in the league this season, one fewer than last season’s leading goalscorer in Ligue 1, Esteban Lepaul.

Toulouse possible starting lineup:.

Restes; Diallo, Koumbassa, Nicolaisen, Tape; Jorgensen, Casseres, Sigur, Russell-Rowe; Vignolo, Tengstedt.

Rennes possible starting lineup:.

Samba; Reynolds, Cresswell, Oliveira, Rouault; Cisse; Al-Taamari, Blas, Camara; Dia, Lepaul.

As much as they have struggled of late, we believe Rennes' firepower will be sharper this weekend and punish a Toulouse backline that is far from reassuring defensively.

‘A team we all respect’ – Jota Silva and Pirola preview Milan test for Olympiacos

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (655 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Olympiacos duo Jota Silva and Lorenzo Pirola are looking forward to welcoming AC Milan to the Karaiskakis Stadium this evening.
  • Milan travel to the Greek capital hoping to get their Europa League campaign up and running.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Olympiacos duo Jota Silva and Lorenzo Pirola are looking forward to welcoming AC Milan to the Karaiskakis Stadium this evening.

Milan travel to the Greek capital hoping to get their Europa League campaign up and running. They have won just one of their opening four league phase fixtures, which was a 4-0 drubbing of RB Salzburg.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Defeats to Benfica, Bournemouth and Ferencvaros – all without scoring a single goal – have seen the Rossoneri slide into the bottom 12 positions in the table. With only 12 points up for grabs, they must start to put things right. By contrast, Olympiacos have won three of four, and sit sixth.

Recent findings suggest that jota Silva spoke to Gianluca Di Marzio about tonight’s game in Athens, admitting that the Rossoneri are a team that they respect despite their slow start in Europe. His words are via MilanNews.

What kind of game are you expecting?

Recent findings suggest that “It will be a great match, between two teams that usually play in the Champions League. Milan are a well-equipped opponent with an extraordinary history: they are a team we all respect. We are two historic and important teams: they, like us, are having a good season.”.

They only have three points in the Europa League….

Recent findings suggest that “They will certainly want to fight to advance to the next round of the European competition. They have players of excellent quality, including many internationals and many highly experienced players. Amorim is a fantastic coach and needs no introduction.”.

Meanwhile, defender Lorenzo Pirola spoke alongside his head coach Imanol Alguacil at a press conference on the eve of the game.

What’s your message for the fans, who will once again fill the stadium?

Sources indicate that “As with every match, we promise to give it our all this time. We face a tough opponent. It’s another crucial match, and we have a very significant evening ahead of us. We want to finish the game with a win and get the three points.”.

Having come through Inter’s youth academy, do you have any extra motivation for facing Milan?

“In any case, I spent four years at Inter, and it was a very wonderful and important experience. It’s a great experience to be able to play against Milan, but for me the most important thing is the three points from the win. That’s my goal.”.

Does the fact that this is a crucial match for Milan in terms of the league position provide additional motivation for Olympiacos to remain focused?

According to recent reports, “It’s an important match for both Milan and Olympiacos, even though we have ten points. We’ll do everything we can to get the points we need to win and reach thirteen. We’ll give our all to achieve that.”.

Could this match also be a calling card for you for the Italian national team? Also, how much have Milan changed since you faced them with Inter?

“Considering that I’ve been here for almost three years and that my career is going well, I don’t see the match against Milan as a positive or negative opportunity for the national team.

Industry observers note that “Milan are always a dangerous team and has a good squad. Anything can happen in a match, and as I’ve said before, we’ll do everything we can to win.”.

What do you expect from Milan in tomorrow’s match, and how do you see them competing for the title?

According to recent reports, “It will be a tough and intense match, with both teams pressing hard. I think it will be a very close game, and we’ll try to give our best. As for the league, everything is still open. We’re only at the start of the season, so I can’t give a precise assessment right now.”.

Auxerre vs Marseille - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (613 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joel Lefevre | 27 Nov 2026 02:00.
  • Auxerre will try to put some more distance between themselves and the relegation zone as they wrap up November by welcoming Marseille to Stade de l’Abbe-Deschamps on Sunday.
  • After 11 matchdays, the Burgundy club sit 15th in the Ligue 1 table, drawing Monaco 1-1 the last time out, with OM right now in fifth following to a 3-2 defeat at Le Mans.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 27 Nov 2026 02:00.

Auxerre will try to put some more distance between themselves and the relegation zone as they wrap up November by welcoming Marseille to Stade de l’Abbe-Deschamps on Sunday.

After 11 matchdays, the Burgundy club sit 15th in the Ligue 1 table, drawing Monaco 1-1 the last time out, with OM right now in fifth following to a 3-2 defeat at Le Mans.

After a rough start to the 2026-27 campaign, it appears as though Auxerre are doing just enough to get by domestically.

Will Still’s men lost their first three matches of this top-flight season, but have since collected points in six of their last eight league fixtures.

That has them just a point above Strasbourg who are in the relegation playoff spot heading into matchday 12 with Auxerre just three points above Angers, who are in the last automatic relegation position.

So far this season AJA have yet to lose a Ligue 1 fixture when netting the opening goal, with their draw versus Monaco last week being the first time they dropped points in that position.

They lead the league regarding fouls per match (16.1) while allowing the joint-most goals in this competition after 11 matchdays (25).

AJA have points in three of their last four Ligue 1 fixtures at home, with their last win at Stade de l’Abbe-Deschamps occuring in September against Brest (2-1).

Marseille will hope their late collapse against Le Mans serves as a temporary speed bump and a wake-up call going forward.

Bruno Genesio’s side bounced back well in midweek, defeating Levski Sofia 1-0 in Europa League action, putting them into the knockout places in that competition.

Clean sheets like the one they collected on Thursday have been rare for OM in Ligue 1, as they have conceded a 2.40 xG average following their defeat to Le Mans in the top flight.

Fortunately, they are balancing that out with plenty of goals, averaging the second-most goals per game in Ligue 1 (2.2) heading into matchday 12.

After 11 matchdays, only three points presently separate them from the top three and a place in next season’s Champions League.

Les Olympiens will seek a third successive triumph versus Auxerre in this competition, having won both Ligue 1 meetings against them last season 1-0.

Marseille form (all competitions):.

Both Bryan Okoh and Assane Diousse will miss this match for Auxerre as they recover from cruciate ligament tears, while Sekou Fofana has a groin strain and Danny Loader is questionable with an ankle injury.

Romain Faivre scored their only goal on matchday 11, the second of the campaign for the man currently on loan from Bournemouth.

At Marseille, Derek Cornelius is still recovering from a hip problem, Emerson Palmieri is questionable with a knee injury and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg is questionable because of an illness.

Amine Gouiri scored the winner in their Europa League victory on Thursday, becoming the first OM player to net in five successive competitive fixtures since Florian Thauvin in 2018, while he and Igor Paixao scored in their defeat to Le Mans.

Auxerre possible starting lineup:.

Nardi; Diomande, Tuanzebe, Siwe; Senaya, Ahamada, Danois, Oppegard; Faivre, Lascary; Archer.

Marseille possible starting lineup:.

De Lange; Weah, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Garcia; Kamissoko, Nnadi; Gomes, Maupay, Paixao; Gouiri.

These are two of the most inconsistent defensive units in the league, and in a match which could be wide open for that reason, we believe the quality of the visitors, who have fared well in those kinds of matches this season, will enable them to prevail.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last aturday’s 2-0 defeat at Broadbridge Heath was the latest serback in a run which has left them in sixth spot – so still in the play-off places but now nine points behind leaders Faversham.

Their next bie to emerge from their tricky run comes at ninth-placed Punjab United – and they’ve been boosted by the arrival of ex-Crowborough goal ace Ellioot Duncan, although have lost Mitch Chapman to Margate.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It has been revealed that dolan dissected the week’s events with us and said: “You’d have to say Broadbridge Heath deserved the win. First half, I don’t think they caused us too many problems. Momentum is key – like when you’re doing well and a goal goes in against you, which was an unfortunate error from Harry (Haines). It just went under his hand – there wasn’t much power in it from 20 yards.

According to recent reports, "I’m not going to hold that against Harry, he’s been good for us this season. But when things aren’t going for you, little things like that go against you. It kills the momentum you had in the game and it does knock the stuffing out of people a bit.

"Without being disrespectful, I didn’t really see that Broadbridge Heath caused us too many problems, not until the second half when we were 2-0 down and chasing it – they probably could have scored a few more then.

Industry observers note that "We chucked bodies forward, we had four strikers on the pitch. We had chances but there was maybe only one that was clear-cut in the second half which we needed to do better with.

Industry observers note that "At the moment we are in bad form. It does happen in football – teams don’t win week in, week out, especially at this level, or even at the top level in the Premier League.

"This level is definitely more inconsistent this year. You can see from results, anybody can beat anybody.

It has been revealed that "You’ve just got to stay on it and that’s what we’re doing with the boys in training – back to basics, try to keep things simple, don’t over-complicate things, try to make the right decisions, get in the right areas. We’re working hard on putting it right.

"Our boys are prepared for that, we’ve been going through it in training.

"Once we do get a win I genuinely think we’ll be okay. It’s about getting confidence back – and winning games gives you confidence.

"I’ve still got confidence in this squad. If you look at what we did in those fist 10 or 15 games, there’s no reason why we can’t go on another good winning run with the squad we have, with one or two additions.".

On addition already on board is hotshot Duncan, who made significant FA Cup scoring headlines with the Crows earlier in the season.

"You have to have freshness and competition for places and we’re trying to add to the squad for competition in areas where we feel we need it,” Dolan stated.

"Elliott coming in is great competition for the frontline boys. He can play anywhere acorss the frontline and knows the level really well. He’s very good with the ball at his feet and knows where the goal is. He’ll get firing for us.

"He came in for his debut (at Heath) not really knowing any of the boys and will need a game or two to get up to speed with how we play.".

According to recent reports, of Chapman’s switch to league rivals Margate, Dolan said: "Mitch has moved on. We have had three approaches for him in the time we have had him, from step three and step four, and this one was in line with where he lives and where they train.

"Mitch did a great job for us – he filled in for me when I was injured – but players move and I have a lot of time for Mitch and have no glitch with him moving on.

It has been revealed that "We’re hoping to have another one or two added to the squad ready for Saturday. Hopefully we can get them over the line and move on and get the win Saturday.”.

Hastingsknow a visit to Punjab United will not be easy. Dolan remarked: “It will be a hard game away from home. I’ve played there and their pitch is on a bit of a slope. "They’re a very substantial, physical, direct side, from what I know.”.

The club noted: “Current Year 11 students can combine their passion for football with study towards a Level 3 qualification in Sport and Physical Activity.

“Based at Three Bridges FC in Crawley, the programme offers UEFA-qualified coaching, competitive fixtures and structured education in partnership with JACE Training. Teaching and football coaching will be led by Jamie Crellin, an experienced teacher of 10 years and the club’s First Team Manager.

“Our ambition is to develop talented footballers while helping young people gain the qualifications, skills and confidence needed for their future.”.

The club are holding their first Open Trial & Information Evening on Wednesday 16 December 2026, from 5pm–8pm, at Three Bridges FC.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 10:33 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 04:18 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • The voice of the late BBC commentator John Motson will be featured on the EA Sports FC 27 video game through 'a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation'.
  • Motson, who died at the age of 77 in 2023, had served as the lead commentator on BBC's football coverage for decades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 10:33 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 04:18 EST, 26 November 2026.

The voice of the late BBC commentator John Motson will be featured on the EA Sports FC 27 video game through 'a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation'.

Motson, who died at the age of 77 in 2023, had served as the lead commentator on BBC's football coverage for decades.

The legendary commentator had also lent his voice to Electronic Arts's FIFA series of games in the 1990s and 2000s.

EA has declared that it has worked with the blessing and in partnership with Motson's family to have him feature as an optional commentary selection in an enhancement of the latest edition of their EA Sports FC game.

The publisher stated its development studio 'has put Motson back into the commentary box with the aid of new AI-tools, bringing a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation trained by recordings of the man himself.'.

EA said its team worked with 'extensive care and respect to create a digital tribute to one of the game's greatest voices'.

The late BBC commentator John Motson will feature on the EA Sports FC 27 video game, through recordings and AI recreation.

Motson's family gave permission for the late commentator, who died in 2023, to feature in the game.

'My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA SPORTS FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game,' said Fred Motson, son of John Motson.

'His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole new set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary.'.

Motson's son also told the BBC his father would have 'absolutely' wanted to be involved in the game after his death.

The BBC reported that Motson's family were paid for the rights to use his likeness and to recreate his voice in the game.

EA added that AI had been the 'only way' for Motson's voice to feature, as there were no recordings of him talking about modern players.

While Motson's family gave EA's project their blessing, the use of AI to recreate voices has become an increasingly controversial topic.

In August, a group of 80 performers backed the Save Our Voices Now campaign, which is seeking to secure legal protection against technology which can clone a person's voice and make it say anything its operator chooses.

The campaign was founded by actor and voice artist Peter Caulfield and has been backed by stars including Hugh Bonneville, Nicola Coughlan and Matt Lucas.

Campaigners want Britain to follow the example set by Denmark, which has moved to give its citizens full legal control over AI-generated imitations of their face, body and voice.

The protections allow people to demand that any unauthorised content is removed and seek compensation for its misuse.

Crawley extended their unbeaten run in the league under Blackwell to four games with a 0-0 draw at home to title contenders Barnet in midweek – and Blackwell now believes that his side are “competitive” – not only on the eye but also according to the data.

Sources indicate that the former Sheffield United manager noted: “The data shows that we're very competitive now with sprints, decelerations, accelerations, high-speed runs. We're now coming at the top half of the table with that so it just shows that we've been improving all over.”.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

From a defensive point of view the past two games have shown a rejuvenated back-line – helped by the recent additions of Ben Heneghan and Josh Flint, which have made the Reds look a lot more resolute and solid.

Exeter are currently one spot below the play-off places sitting in 8th place on 23 points. The Grecians have the best defensive record in the league having only conceded 10 goals but Blackwell is not fazed by that.

It has been revealed that he has communicated as much to his players: “It doesn't matter whether they're the top or the bottom, we feel now that we can compete with people, and that's all I wanted to do, make us competitive. Then hopefully Lady Luck smiles on you on the day and you can get some good results.”.

Blackwell was pleased that more players have stepped up to the mark to give him more confidence in choices.

He said: “We talk about how any team wants to be competitive from 1-22 really, and know that if you lose a player, that someone can seamlessly step in. What was pleasing was that we made some changes, shifted it around a little bit, and then whoever we brought in did a good job, so that gives me more power.”.

With the Reds involved in a lunchtime kick-off, Blackwell was asked whether that makes a difference to the way they approach the game.

He replied: “I think it's something that I've been used to now for the last 15 years, you know, being in a Championship or the Premier League and abroad in Poland is exactly the same.

“You don't know whether you're playing a Friday, a Saturday, a Sunday or a Monday, they're the four days that you normally play.

“You don't know whether you're going to be at 12 o'clock, 2pm, 4pm, 8pm – so it's now it's just normal for players; it certainly has been for me. So nothing different, whatever the time is, we'll prepare as if it were a 3pm kick-off or a 1pm kick-off. Preparation is the same.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.
  • By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.
  • Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Industry observers note that rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Recent findings suggest that bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Industry observers note that equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

Recent findings suggest that “We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager mentioned. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

It has been revealed that it does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Recent findings suggest that marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

Recent findings suggest that united fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

According to recent reports, spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

Recent findings suggest that it had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick stated: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”.

In a recent development, when asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

If Manchester City had not entered a legal battle with the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching 114 charges relating to financial regulations by an independent panel, then surely there would be more pressure on the two head coaches in the dugout this evening?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 02:11.

Chelsea are understood to be monitoring Boca Juniors centre-back Facundo Herrera after the defender’s swift emergence in South American football.

The 20-year-old, known in Argentina as ‘Jagger’ because of his likeness to Rolling Stones singer Mick Jagger, has made remarkable strides over the last four months.

After making his senior bow in August, the former captain of Boca’s reserve side swiftly established himself in the first team and helped the club win the Copa Sudamericana in Barranquilla last week.

Herrera impressed in the 2-0 final triumph over Atletico Mineiro, completing 56 of 58 passes and recording nine clearances as Boca kept a clean sheet.

Argentine publications El Crack Deportivo and Clarin via Sport Witness report that Chelsea scouts are closely assessing Herrera's physical and technical progress as part of the club’s continuing recruitment drive in South America.

The 1.80m right-footer has earned plaudits for his speed, aerial strength and composure when playing through the opposition’s press from the back.

Herrera indicated his eye for a decisive moment on October 25 by scoring his first senior goal with a late winner against Independiente that secured Boca's place at the top of the annual league standings.

The youngster's growing standing has attracted praise from some of Argentina’s most respected figures: Boca's record appearance-maker Roberto Mouzo has likened him to 1978 World Cup winner Alberto Tarantini, while Oscar Ruggeri has called on national team manager Lionel Scaloni to give him senior minutes straight away.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea are not the only club following the youngster. Barcelona are reportedly seeking scouting reports ahead of January, while Benfica, Borussia Dortmund and Porto have also been linked with him.

Despite increasing interest from England and elsewhere in Europe, a move to prise Herrera away from La Bombonera in 2027 is unlikely to be straightforward.

Boca president Juan Roman Riquelme is determined to keep the heart of his trophy-winning squad together as the club prepare for next year's Copa Libertadores.

Head coach Rodolfo Arruabarrena has also told the board he wants the defender to stay, praising his strength in one-on-one duels and his willingness to learn from more experienced team-mates.

Boca have yet to receive a formal offer or begin transfer talks, putting the club in a strong position to resist early approaches while Herrera continues to develop in Buenos Aires.

According to recent reports, the club’s decision to go for a change at the top has caused a huge amount of upset – with many fans saying it is a shocking decision and a number of Macdonald’s squad deciding to follow him out of the door. And it is the way the decision appears to have been handled that has caused the most anger.

As the week unfolded, Town – who are second from bottom of the Isthmian South East division after only two wins in 19 games – appointed club stalwart Dave Winterton as interim manager, with senior player Arron Hopkinson assisting him, and asked fans to get behind him.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

And they put out an advert inviting applicants for the job, with talk of them wanting to take the whole club – not just the men’s first team – forward as one.

Macdonald’s right-hand man Ben Davis has gone in the wake of the sacking and so, reportedly, have long-serving Adam Davidson and at least five players.

Macdonald gave an exclusive interview to the Eastbourne Herald and sussexworld.co.uk in which he remarked he had been told eight days before he was sacked that his job was ‘bomb-proof’ all the time the chairman was in place.

It has been revealed that he also noted he had learned the club had decided they wanted a change of manager on November 16 – and only after two more games, training and two more siginings did they tell him. Macdonald told us he was asked if would resign, but refused.

Industry observers note that you can read our full interview with Macdonald, who has been at the helm since 2022, on pages 62 & 63. He finished it with these words: “You don’t often get the chance to manage the club from the town you grew up in and I’ve just committed over 10% of my life to it, so the next few days and weeks will just be reflecting on that and appreciating the opportunity that the club gave me four-and-a-half years ago, and the continued and consistent success we have given them in return.”.

As for what happens next, Winterton isinterim manager and the Town committee have asked fans to get behind him as he guides the squad through what will be a tricky period.

The immediate aim is to try to get out of the Isthmian SE danger zone, and that starts with a visit to Erith Town tomorrow, followed by a home Sussex derby with Broadbridge Heath a week later.

Those won’t be easy games with a number of Macdonald’s players announcing they also left – including James Waters, who had only rejoined the club a day before the manager was ousted.

Industry observers note that meanwhile the club – who gave ‘sincere thanks’ to Macdonald in their statement revealing he was leaving – are inviting applicants for the vacancy. They remarked: “We are looking for an individual who shares our ambition, understands the importance of building a strong club culture and is passionate about developing players, creating opportunities and delivering success both on and off the pitch.

Industry observers note that "At Eastbourne Town, we believe the First Team should be an notable part of a wider football development pathway. We want to create an environment where young players can see a realistic route from youth football through U18 and U23 football and ultimately into the first team.”.

I watched Celtic leave it late in Portugal and noted gamble pay off, emotional homecoming and serious concern

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1077 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Scotsman

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Unconvincing Celtic kept their Europa League qualification hopes alive with a hard-fought and historic 2-1 victory over Portuguese second-tier side Torreense.
  • Martin O’Neill’s men took an early lead through a Javi Vazquez own goal after nine minutes, but Dany Jean restored parity for the hosts before half-time in Leiria.
  • Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unconvincing Celtic kept their Europa League qualification hopes alive with a hard-fought and historic 2-1 victory over Portuguese second-tier side Torreense.

Martin O’Neill’s men took an early lead through a Javi Vazquez own goal after nine minutes, but Dany Jean restored parity for the hosts before half-time in Leiria.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The visitors struggled to find a breakthrough after the interval, until substitute Camilo Duran rose unmarked to head home James Forrest’s cross in the 84th minute.

The late winner secured a second consecutive victory in the competition for Celtic, moving them on to six points from five matches and up to 25th in the league-phase standings after keeping their hopes of reaching the knockout stages alive.

It was also the Scottish champions’ victory win on Portuguese soil since 2003.

Lewis Anderson watched the action unfold for The Scotsman and picks out his four main takeaways from the game.

Celtic may have made unnecessarily hard work of beating a Portuguese second division outfit right now sitting 13th in their league, but Martin O’Neill will care little about the aesthetics after securing three precious points.

Sources indicate that although Celtic enjoyed plenty of possession after the interval, their use of the ball was frequently pedestrian, with too many passes going sideways or backwards rather than putting Torreense under meaningful pressure. There were spells when Celtic appeared destined to settle for a frustrating draw, but ultimately they have given themselves a genuine opportunity to reach the play-off round and, at this stage of their European campaign, that is what matters most.

Industry observers note that once again, Camilo Duran proved to be the difference-maker. O’Neill's decision to keep the in-form striker in reserve paid dividends, with the substitute delivering the decisive moment when Celtic needed a spark. The Colombian’s back-post header from fellow replacement James Forrest’s pinpoint delivery was precisely the injection of quality that had been missing for much of the evening.

According to recent reports, when the ball arrived at his feet, his first touch was outstanding, allowing him to open his body and switch the play. He then demonstrated the instincts of a natural goal scorer, occupying defenders before finding the space to deliver the decisive finish. Duran may have had only 12 touches, but the one that mattered most was emphatic. He is becoming Celtic's go-to man in crucial moments, and delivered once more when it counted.

Although Jota did not manage to get his name on the scoresheet or provide an assist, his performance in Portugal offered plenty of telltale signs that he is rediscovering the devastating form that once made him such an exciting attacking presence for Celtic. The winger looked particularly at home on his return to familiar surroundings, relishing the chance to perform in front of friends and family after an arduous period on the sidelines.

Sources indicate that making his first European appearance since Celtic’s Champions League disappointment against Bayern Munich in February 2025, the 27-year-old revealed few signs of rustiness despite two injury-disrupted seasons. He was a constant menace to Torreense down the left flank, using his pace, close control and willingness to take on defenders to cause problems throughout his time on the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that his influence was particularly evident during the opening period, creating two opportunities, testing the goalkeeper twice and delivering a succession of enticing crosses that deserved more decisive finishing from his team-mates. One such delivery contributed to Celtic's opening goal, when Vazquez inadvertently turned the ball into his own net.

Given the length of his absence and the physical demands of returning to elite-level football, there had been understandable questions over whether Jota could recapture the explosive qualities that previously made him a favourite among the Celtic support. His latest display provided a really encouraging response. There is still work to do before he reaches his previous heights, but the signs are increasingly promising.

Sources indicate that this success has breathed fresh life into Celtic's European campaign, but O’Neill will be under no illusions that there is considerable scope for improvement if his side are to make further progress. Individual contributions may have rescued the evening in Portugal, yet they should not disguise some worrying collective shortcomings, particularly the vulnerability of the defence and the lack of composure when chances presented themselves in the final third.

The format offers Celtic a route into the knockout stages, with the top eight in the league phase advancing automatically to the last 16, while those finishing between ninth and 24th must negotiate a two-legged play-off. There remains little margin for error, though, with three fixtures remaining. Celtic still have Omonoia, Marseille and current league-phase leaders Union Saint-Gilloise to negotiate, and will almost certainly require further points if they are to extend their European journey.

There is, however, reason for optimism. The win over Torreense means Celtic have now recorded successive wins in a major European competition for the first time since defeating Ferencvaros home and away during the 2021-22 group stage of this tournament. It is a positive milestone for O’Neill's side and another indication that, despite their problems, Celtic are beginning to build some momentum at a crucial stage.

It has been revealed that torreense may have been unfancied on paper, but they demonstrated they were no pushovers and gave Celtic a considerably sterner test than their second-tier status might have suggested. The Portuguese outfit were organised, and disciplined, refusing to be overawed by the occasion or the gulf in resources between the two clubs.

In a recent development, joão Nuno’s side pressed aggressively, competed well for second balls and indicated enough attacking ambition to expose some of Celtic's defensive vulnerabilities. Their equaliser was reward for an approach that refused to crumble after falling behind, while their resistance after the interval threatened to frustrate the visitors further.

Celtic's superior individual quality eventually told, but Torreense deserve credit for making them dig deep for the result. This was no routine European assignment. For all the criticism Celtic will face over aspects of their performance, Torreense should not be dismissed as cannon fodder. They demonstrated spirit and sufficient quality to suggest their lowly league position told only part of the story.

Since taking over, the Reds are unbeaten in four in the league, and despite dropping out of both cup competitions in the space of three days, there has been a mentality shift in the players – and the fans have seen that the players are giving their all.

Despite Christmas just being around the corner, the club hope Reds fans travel in their numbers to Exter to cheer the boys on in an early kick off. But it has been noted that Blackwell doesn’t celebrate with the players like past managers have.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Speaking in his pre-Exeter press conference, Blackwell remarked one or two fans asked him why he didn’t go and thank the support: “I thank the fans all the time, but after the game, it’s vital that the players get the credit, not the manager.

According to recent reports, “That’s not my job. My job is to try to prepare the team, and the players go out and give everything. If they do that, that’s what the fans want. They don’t want me walking up and down the pitch clapping and whatever. Get on, do your job Blackwell, do your job. And if that’s the case, the players are doing well.”.

He added: “It’s not my style. I enjoy them enjoying it and I enjoy that the fans enjoy it. I’ve had a great career, managing massive clubs and been a long way in big competitions, been all over the world, and I’ve never wanted the adulation.

“I just enjoy other people having it and seeing my players get that and the fans enjoying it. Sending them home after a week’s work, seeing the players give everything. That’s what they want. If we can keep doing that, I think we keep them on-side.”.

Talking about the bond between players and fans, Blackwell said “I want the players to take the credit because the bond is between the players and the fans, and that’s the bond.

"As an ex-player, I knew there was a great bond between me and the fans. I’d hate to think that the manager walked up and started taking my thunder after having a man of the match performance and he walks up and takes all the credit. No, I want the players to have the credit.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Derek McInnes has revealed that he used Jamestown Analytics to rate Rangers' signing of Ryan Naderi while manager of Hearts last season.

Hearts gained access to Jamestown's treasure trove of player recruitment data in 2024 after selling a stake in the club to the man who formed the company, Brighton chairman Tony Bloom.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

While used primarily to source signings for their own squad, Hearts are also able to access information on signings made by their Premiership rivals.

McInnes admitted that he ran Naderi through the system and was left hoping that Rangers would not sign the Czech striker as he was identified as a good signing for the Ibrox club.

He explained: "Last January, obviously, when we first seen that Rangers were linked with Naderi, like everyone else, I would say to [Hearts sporting director] Graeme Jones, 'How do they rate him?'.

According to recent reports, "Because you're always curious. It's just the way it is. It's brilliant when you see other teams round about you signing a player that's not rated. That's the way it was. It's just natural.

According to recent reports, "But no, he was someone that I think was well known to them. I think Brugge had an interest in Ryan, and I think USG potentially had an interest in him as well. But the kind of money, the fee, it just kind of went away for them, I think.

Sources indicate that "But we were told that he was a good player before I'd even set eyes on him. The feeling was that he was somebody that could help Rangers and make them better. So when I'd seen a lot of the comings and goings, it was on, it was off, it was off, on again, I was kind of hoping that it would fall through, being the Hearts manager. But when I'd seen they'd signed him, I knew that Rangers had strengthened. And I think Rangers did strengthen well in January last year.

Recent findings suggest that "So that was the first we kind of looked a wee bit more at him but, again, you just do it as an opposition manager, looking at him. It's only when you get to work with people on a daily basis that you get to see them.".

Naderi initially struggled to live up to his £4.75million transfer tag after joining Rangers in January from German third tier side Hansa Rostock.

However, the 23-year-old has emerged as a talismanic figure this season, scoring 10 goals in his last 20 games and providing the focal point in attack following injuries to Youssef Chermiti and Lawrence Shankland.

"I had a good conversation with Ryan when I first came in the door about what we felt this season could look like for him," McInnes noted. "Because it's not always easy for a young player settling in January and they're in the middle of a race, but to try and really establish himself this season.

"I think he stood up brilliantly to a couple of the senior injuries, to other injuries throughout, to Youssef and Lawrence. He's had to be the guy and he's led the line brilliantly. I love the goals he scores. I love his work rate anyway. But it's nice that people don't just see him as a grafter now and a worker. He's actually got good intelligence.

"All top strikers have intelligence to be in the right place at the right time and it's symptomatic of some of the goals he scores, following things in, just always believing there might just be something there for me.

According to recent reports, "I love having a striker that has the ability to score those types of goals. But he leads the line well, gets us up the pitch and works ever so hard, as you know. He's done well. He should feel pleased. I think the fact that he's got capped as well, he's taken a real step on from that. I think he's taken a lot of confidence from that.

"However he gets his confidence, whether it's scoring goals, whether it's staying fit, being a significant part of the team, whether it's getting recognised at international level, we all want it to continue.".

Industry observers note that and Washington noted he things Blackwell is a good appointment and believes he can turn things round. “I can understand the decision to go with someone like Kevin Blackwell until the end of the season. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 02:29, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 02:31.

Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United are reportedly facing a fee of at least €80m (£67m) if they are to tempt teenage defender Joane Gadou away from Borussia Dortmund.

The 19-year-old French centre-back has made a swift breakthrough in Germany after joining from Red Bull Salzburg for €20m (£16.8m) last summer.

Dortmund believe they have found another exceptional prospect with the potential to make his mark on the international stage, and his estimated market value has reportedly already risen by 40% to €28m (£23.5m) according to Sport Witness.

The former Paris Saint-Germain academy player, recently linked with Liverpool, is under contract for the long term and has no release clause, leaving the Bundesliga club firmly in control of his future.

The leading Premier League clubs are likely to have stepped up their interest after Gadou delivered a commendable performance in Tuesday's 1-1 Champions League draw with Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

Viktor Gyokeres put the hosts ahead inside the opening 10 minutes, but Gadou supplied the match’s defining moment in the 55th minute, earning Dortmund a valuable point.

The teenager surged forward from his own half, fended off two Arsenal challenges and played a decisive pass for Maximilian Beier to equalise.

In his 89 minutes in North London, Gadou also made four clearances and completed 19 of his 22 passes, drawing warm praise from head coach Niko Kovac.

According to recent reports, "We signed him because he is composed in possession and can contribute going forward," Kovac remarked. "He can break the lines and regularly create chances for the strikers. He is also very quick with the ball. It was a truly impressive performance.”.

Bild via Sport Witness reports that Dortmund will not consider offers below four times the €20m (£16.8m)they paid Salzburg only months ago.

The club’s firm position is intended to discourage bids in January as Kovac's side aim to retain their key players for the second half of the 2026-27 campaign.

Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United are not the only clubs linked with the Frenchman: former side Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid are also reportedly interested.

Games involving Celtic, Rangers and Hearts in January and February 2027 have been given fresh dates and kick-off times after being selected by broadcasters.

The match beween Falkirk and Hearts on Saturday, January 23, has been moved back to a later 5.45pm kick-off for live coverage on Premier Sports.

St Mirren v Celtic has been pushed back 24 hours to Sunday, January 24, with a 3pm kick off and will be shown live on Sky Sports.

Aberdeen will host Rangers under the Pittodrie lights on Friday, January 29, at 8pm after the match was brought forward at the request of Sky Sports.

Hearts will host St Mirren at Tynecastle on Saturday, January 30, live on Premier Sports, with a 5.45pm kick-off.

A full Premiership fixture card takes place on Wednesday, February 3, with the match between Motherwell and Celtic pushed back by 15 minutes.

The game at Fir Park will now start at 8pm in front of the Sky Sports cameras.

In addition, BBC Scotland has picked up the rights to show Greenock Morton v Partick Thistle with the game moved to Friday, January 22, kick-off 7.30pm.

BBC ALBA will also show Cove Rangers v Ross County with the match now taking place on Saturday, January 30 at 5.30pm.

Winger Osman scored twice – his first goals for the Seagulls – and also provided an assist in Thursday evening’s 4-0 Conference League win over Romanian champions Universitatea Craiova.

The 21-year-old has been limited to 41 minutes of top-flight action across four substitute appearances this season after being loaned to Feyenoord, Auxerre and Birmingham since his 2024 arrival from Danish club Nordsjaelland.

“It’s not always the fact that he has to do more; sometimes the players who are currently on the pitch do a lot to stay on the pitch,” noted Hurzeler.

“Therefore he needs to keep working hard, he needs to be patient, he needs to be there when we need him.

“We have plenty of games in the next weeks and I always emphasise that we need the full squad, that we need everyone, everyone will play an notable role for us.

“No matter how many minutes you play, you need to contribute to the success for this club and we need to always put the team first. Some players might have to be a little bit more patient but in the right moment you need to be there so you have to always be ready and alive to support the team.”.

Brighton, who sit second in the Premier League, will look to bounce back from last weekend’s surprise 2-0 defeat at Hull when they host Newcastle on Sunday.

Arsenal transfer news: Championship club prepare offer for Ethan Nwaneri, underused at Dortmund

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 27 Nov 2026 06:25.
  • Ethan Nwaneri was the breakout star of Arsenal's 2024-25 season, but he has endured a difficult period for several months.
  • In a recent development, short of game time at Arsenal, the 19-year-old Englishman was loaned to Marseille in the second half of last season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 27 Nov 2026 06:25.

Ethan Nwaneri was the breakout star of Arsenal's 2024-25 season, but he has endured a difficult period for several months.

In a recent development, short of game time at Arsenal, the 19-year-old Englishman was loaned to Marseille in the second half of last season. It was an underwhelming spell, during which the winger started only four times and was labelled a flop.

This season, Arsenal decided to send him out on loan again, this time to Borussia Dortmund.

In a recent development, however, the England Under-21 international no longer really features in the plans of Niko Kovac. Although he was used on many occasions at the start of the season, Nwaneri has not been in Dortmund's starting line-up since 17 October, away to Union Berlin (0-0).

Since that game, he has made a string of appearances in the final minutes of matches and has been left on the bench for the big games, against Bayern Munich (2-2) and Arsenal (1-1).

As a result, the player, who belongs to Arsenal, has played only 29 minutes in the German club's last seven outings, which is insufficient game time. This situation could also benefit West Ham United.

According to FootballTransfers, West Ham are preparing a loan offer to bring Nwaneri to the club in January.

Sources indicate that the London club, 13th in the Championship, are looking to strengthen their squad in an attempt to return to the Premier League. However, the deal is far from straightforward, as Arsenal will first have to recall their youngster from Dortmund.

The British outlet points out that Nwaneri's loan at Borussia Dortmund does not include an option or obligation to buy. Arsenal have a recall clause which gives them the possibility of bringing their youngster back in January.

Industry observers note that however, the Bundesliga leaders paid a loan fee, reportedly between £3.4m and £4.3m (€4m-€5m), and are covering the player's wages. Therefore, if Arsenal activate the recall clause for Nwaneri, they would have to reimburse the loan fee to Borussia Dortmund.

It therefore remains to be seen whether Arsenal will be prepared to give up that compensation to allow their talented youngster to join an environment more conducive to his progress, and whether the London club will demand another paid loan this winter.

West Ham are, in any case, lurking and ready to position themselves for the deal.

#165077. Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

📅 28 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 35m • 📚 Deep Dive (6927 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 35 min read (6927 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~35 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) has emerged as the predominant form of heart failure worldwide and is increasingly associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes and systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) has emerged as the predominant form of heart failure worldwide and is increasingly associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes and systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. This cardiometabolic HFpEF entity can be conceptualized as a mechanistically defined endotype marked by endothelial dysfunction, metabolic inflexibility and maladaptive inter-organ signalling involving the liver, kidney, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. The cardiometabolic endotype often corresponds to a clinically recognizable adiposity-related clinical phenotype. Despite the growing prevalence of cardiometabolic HFpEF, therapeutic progress has lagged. This is mostly because the classification structure used is based on a commonly over-interpreted biomarker—ejection fraction—although inadequate trial end points and a lack of mechanism-guided precision also have a role. Here we review the evolving epidemiology, mechanistic underpinnings and emerging therapeutic landscape of cardiometabolic HFpEF. We highlight limitations in current diagnostic criteria, the role of extracardiac drivers and the need for soft end points and systems-based modelling. Advances in '-omics', phenotyping and cross-disciplinary frameworks now offer a pathway towards mechanistically targeted interventions that could enable symptomatic control by modifying validated disease mechanisms that culminate in this syndrome.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Celtic have defended their head of security and the action taken against the Green Brigade last season after the fan group declared that four supporters had been cleared over the incident that sparked a lengthy ban.

A statement from the ultras group stated the four had been “finally cleared of wrongdoing” over the incident, which took place during a game against Falkirk on October 25 last year.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The group accused Celtic of “smearing” them with their statement on November 7 last year, which outlined an indefinite ban on about 250 supporters that eventually lasted nearly six months.

Celtic had written that about 100 Green Brigade members took part in an “orchestrated” attempt to prevent an individual being arrested following an incident with a steward and that the large group “verbally abused and assaulted the steward and police officers”.

A Green Brigade statement read: “Not guilty pleas were accepted by both Procurator Fiscal and sheriff for breach of the peace charges before the trial commenced.

“The four supporters cleared were subjected to dawn raids, damage to homes and harassment of family members including confiscation of personal devices, this included a vulnerable adult who was left alone in the cold with no means to contact anyone after the front door was removed.”.

The group called for Celtic to apologise for the collective ban and to lift suspensions on two supporters who remain banned over their interaction with the club’s head of security, Mark Hargreaves, at last year’s abandoned annual general meeting.

“This week’s outcome represents significant vindication for all supporters concerned in these events over the past year,” they added.

“It also calls into question the credibility of Mark Hargreaves’ subsequent allegations against two Green Brigade representatives.

Industry observers note that “We maintain that Mark Hargreaves has introduced a poisonous security culture to Celtic Park and does not hold the trust of supporters whose safety he is supposed to be responsible for. His position is untenable.”.

According to recent reports, celtic pointed out they play no part in criminal proceedings and added that they were not aware all had been completed. And they stated that the outcome of the four cases did not alter their assessment of the incident.

A statement added: “The conduct of the group witnessed that day was unsafe and completely unacceptable – it has no place at Celtic Park or anywhere in football. The club took reasonable and proportionate steps to deal with this conduct.

“Such was the seriousness of the incident that the club was called to attend a special meeting of the Safety Advisory Group of Glasgow City Council.”.

Celtic accused the Green Brigade of continuing a “campaign of personal harassment and abuse” towards former senior police officer Hargreaves.

They added: “Mark is a highly-qualified, dedicated professional who plays a crucial role at the club in ensuring the safety of our supporters.

“Where conduct presents an unacceptable risk to that safety or demonstrates an unwillingness to co-operate with it, the club has to take appropriate and proportionate action.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brighton still require six more points to guarantee their place in the last 16 of the Uefa Conference League following Thursday night's impressive 4-0 victory over Romanian league leaders Craiova.

Fabian Hurzeler's side are at the moment second in the league phase table - behind leaders Monaco - with 10 points from their opening four matches, putting them in a strong position to secure automatic qualification for the knockout stages.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The top eight teams qualify directly for the last 16, while those finishing between ninth and 24th must negotiate an additional knockout play-off round.

Brighton have two league-phase fixtures remaining, starting with a home meeting against leaders Monaco on December 10 before travelling to face Panathinaikos on December 17.

Winning both matches would take the Seagulls to 16 points and guarantee a top-eight finish, regardless of results elsewhere.

Four points from the remaining games would leave them on 14 and extremely well placed, although mathematical qualification would not be certain.

Three points would see them to 13 points and would still have a strong chance, depending on other results.

Hurzeler will be particularly encouraged by Brighton's defensive record, with the Seagulls yet to concede a goal in their four Conference League matches.

The Albion have scored nine times and will now look to finish the league phase strongly and avoid the extra play-off round in February.

Head coach Fabian Hurzeler was delighted with the performance against Craiova.

The German said: “I think that was a really good start, and also very vital to make the game look easy, because especially the first goal helped us force [the opponent] to open up the space,” he said.

It has been revealed that “That meant we could have more space to combine and more opportunity to attack their box. So I think we were very professional with good standards in the first half. Then, of course, the red card definitely helped us to finish - or to change - the structure of the game.

It has been revealed that “In the second half we created plenty of chances. I wasn't happy that we weren't clinical and clean enough finishing these chances, because I think we dropped our level a little bit there. Overall, though, winning 4–0 means that we did a lot of things well.”.

Here are the key dates for the 2026/27 UEFA Conference League knockout stages, should Brighton progress:.

- Knockout play-off round: February 18 and 25, 2027.

- Round of 16: March 11 and 18, 2027.

- Quarter-finals: April 8 and 15, 2027.

- Semi-finals: April 29 and May 6, 2027.

- Final: June 2, 2027 – Beşiktaş Stadium, Istanbul, Turkey.

Fabian Hürzeler gives brilliant answer to Gary Lineker's Brighton title race theory

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gary Lineker argued that the Seagulls could become genuine title contenders – and be ‘very difficult to stop’ – if they had a striker in the mould of former Leicester City forward Jamie Vardy.
  • All-time leading Premier League goalscorer Alan Shearer agreed but also praised the quality of recent performances, including the surprise defeat at Hull City.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gary Lineker argued that the Seagulls could become genuine title contenders – and be ‘very difficult to stop’ – if they had a striker in the mould of former Leicester City forward Jamie Vardy.

All-time leading Premier League goalscorer Alan Shearer agreed but also praised the quality of recent performances, including the surprise defeat at Hull City.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Recent findings suggest that hürzeler insists he is happy with the attacking options already at his disposal, pointing to Brighton’s goalscoring record and the number of players capable of finding the net. Albion lead the Premier League goals scored table, finding the net 26 times in 11 games.

Asked about Lineker and Shearer’s praise for Brighton as one of the most entertaining teams in the league, Hürzeler welcomed the recognition but stressed that performances, rather than outside opinion, must remain the priority.

“If they say this, of course we should listen to it,” he said.

"We should appreciate the opinion.

“On the other side, being the best football team doesn't mean you automatically win games.

In a recent development, “We really have to keep focusing on our performances, that’s what we can control. We can't control what others think about us.

“We can only control how well we prepare for a game and how high our levels are on matchday.

“The truth is always on the pitch, and therefore we have to get back to our highest level.”.

Hürzeler was more emphatic when asked whether he agreed with Lineker’s suggestion that Brighton were missing a clinical, traditional centre-forward.

“An Alan Shearer?” the German replied, tongue-in-cheek.

“No, no. I think we have a lot of good strikers. When you look at how many goals we've scored in the season so far, and how many goals we scored today.

"We might not have one striker but we have plenty of players who are able to score goals.

“That's what has made us strong in the past and what will make us strong in the future, hopefully on Sunday as well.”.

The Brighton head coach was speaking after his side responded to their disappointing 2-0 defeat at Hull City with a 4-0 victory over Craiova in the UEFA Conference League.

Next up is a home match against Newcastle United, in the Premier League, this weekend.

Hürzeler specifically named the attacking players he believes can provide the goals, making clear that he has no concerns about the options available to him.

He added: “We're very happy with Kostoulas. We're very happy with [Georginio] Rutter.

"We're also happy with Tobi [Promise David], who came onto the pitch today against Craiova.”.

The head coach also appeared keen to ensure that the defeat at Hull did not define the assessment of his team's attacking play.

Brighton created opportunities at the MKM Stadium but were unable to find a way past an inspired goalkeeper, in Konstantinos Tzolakis, prompting Lineker to suggest that a striker with Vardy's instincts could make them much harder to stop.

Hürzeler, however, would rather focus on the wider picture than one frustrating afternoon in front of goal.

“We're focusing on the positives,” he stated.

"We are not focusing on one game where we missed a few chances.”.

The 4-0 victory over Craiova offered an immediate reminder of Brighton's goalscoring capabilities, although Hürzeler will now want his players to carry that performance into Sunday's match.

#165064. When St Johnstone’s owner was offered square go by Rangers boss - and the call players still wind him up about

When St Johnstone’s owner was offered square go by Rangers boss - and the call players still wind him up about
