💡 Key Takeaways
  • The amount of health and safety regulations required in the construction business nowadays means Geoff Brown is happy to be free the daily responsibility of running the family firm he established.
  • Recent findings suggest that however, some form of welfare protection might have been helpful at the moment he saw Graeme Souness storming down the corridor towards him.
  • Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The amount of health and safety regulations required in the construction business nowadays means Geoff Brown is happy to be free the daily responsibility of running the family firm he established.

Recent findings suggest that however, some form of welfare protection might have been helpful at the moment he saw Graeme Souness storming down the corridor towards him. “He was threatening to knock my block off,” he recalls.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Recent findings suggest that st Johnstone tea-lady Aggie Moffat had erupted because of the state in which Rangers had left the away dressing-room following a 1-1 draw in February 1991. She made sure Souness knew all about it. Brown was in the boardroom with the directors of both clubs when they heard a “serious commotion” in the foyer. The chairman went outside and was met by Souness, who ‘offered’ to take him outside.

“I did not make a noise of it at the time,” says Brown, who wonders what impact it might have had on Souness’ career had he agreed to take part in the square go the Ibrox manager was suggesting. “David Murray phoned me the following week to thank me for not making a noise about what happened,” he says.

Ownership of St Johnstone – his 38 years at the helm of the club is the longest any individual has owned a professional football club in Scotland in modern times – has afforded Brown, now 83, a ringside seat and very nearly active involvement in so many of the colourful incidents characterising the game in this country.

In a recent development, the Aggie incident is certainly included among those. Despite Brown keeping schtum about the threat from Souness at the time, it’s become one of Scottish football’s most well-rehearsed anecdotes.

In a recent development, rightly so, because the so-called storm in a teacup had profound repercussions. Souness ended up citing the incident as one of the reasons he left Rangers for Liverpool shortly afterwards. Brown, by contrast, has not roamed far. Building houses for others occupied his time. After that proved profitable, it permitted him the luxury of time to devote to saving St Johnstone from the clutches of the receivers.

This was in 1986. The Perth club “were the strongest team in the country”. In other words, they were holding the rest of Scottish football up and were sitting plum last in the pile. One afternoon, shortly after Brown had agreed to take on all the debt, Tayside Safety Committee paid a visit. “There were about ten of them,” he recalls. “And they were put in the boardroom. I said: ‘I am sorry, what are you doing here?’.

Sources indicate that “One replied: ‘We are here to close down the club’. Notices had been given to the previous board that had never been passed on to us. They hadn’t met any of the safety standards at the last inspection, and nothing had been done after the inspections. So they were there to close the club down.”.

Forty years and three major trophies later, Brown can reflect with a degree of satisfaction on his impact on football in his local area. But when he was presented with an Outstanding Contribution Award by first minister John Swinney at the Courier Business awards night in Dundee as recently as October, it was more his success as a housebuilder – he set up GS Brown Construction in 1970 – and charitable work that were being recognised.

Recent findings suggest that as Brown was making his way in the construction business, he and his young family lived in a council house in Tulloch. It looked on to berry fields, owned by a farmer called Bruce McDiarmid.

Industry observers note that around twenty years later, as the new owner of St Johnstone FC, he met McDiarmid to negotiate a land deal. The trouble was, St Johnstone had no money to buy the fields on which it was being proposed they could build a new stadium. Asda’s interest in buying their then stadium, Muirton Park, came to light shortly afterwards.

Sources indicate that brown offered McDiarmid a 20 per cent stake in the club for the land, a deal the farmer’s lawyer advised him to reject. But McDiarmid accepted it. When Asda later offered £5 million for the Muirton Park site Brown cannily persuaded the supermarket firm to cover the cost of the newly introduced stadium instead. Some might still be under the impression, incorrect as it turns out, that McDiarmid gifted the land to St Johnstone, perhaps with the sole condition that they had to name the stadium after him.

Recent findings suggest that “He certainly did not,” states Brown. “One way or the other, it did take a bit of persuading. I went with him to see his lawyer, who was older than Bruce. ‘No,’ the lawyer remarked. ‘You don’t really want that. If you are going to sell it, sell it’. Within a year I had Asda going to give us £5 million for Muirton Park. If you are sitting with 20 per cent of that you are not doing too bad…”.

According to recent reports, brown’s new book is called Building My Life – shades of Alex Ferguson’s Managing My Life – but it could be called The Art of the Deal. It includes lots of wrangling and horse-trading, sometimes involving actual horses (As well as football, Brown is also a renowned racehorse owner). He doesn’t always come out on the right side of such negotiations, such as when the players were negotiating bonuses at the start of the 1998-99 season.

Industry observers note that “That was a disaster,” he states. “The players – Paul Kane, Roddy Grant, Allan Preston – they were at (managing director) Stewart Duff because you always agree the bonuses at the start of the year. They are sitting arguing about bonuses for each potential position. And they come to 4th place. ‘4th place – are you happy with £250,000?’ Stewart asked. ‘Aye, go on then,’ I told him. ‘Now they are asking me for third place,’ he says.

Industry observers note that “I said: ‘Stewart, they will never get third’. He indicates: ‘I agree with you. So should we just give them half a million?’”.

In a recent development, reader, they got third place, qualifying for the Uefa Cup in the process. “To this day the ones like Preston and Kane keep rubbing it in,” Brown says. “They tell me: ‘The one thing you got wrong with St Johnstone is that day you gave us too much money!’.

“At that time, European football meant you ran at a loss. Because you’re hiring planes in the holiday period. Chartering a plane was expensive. Plus the (bonus) money we were paying players.”.

Not that Brown regrets any of it. “It’s what you’re in it for, isn’t it?” he notes. Now out of it after selling his majority stake in the club to Atlanta-based lawyer Adam Webb, he can enjoy attending games such as this weekend’s Tayside derby against Dundee United at Tannadice. At home games he sits in the Geoff Brown Stand. “The best bit is, whatever the scoreline, I can sleep afterwards,” he says.

Stewardship of a football club can take a toll, clearly. But Brown made some good friends, none better than Paul Sturrock. Of all the managers he employed, he was the one with whom he shared the closest relationship, to the extent that Brown’s wife Joyce regarded him as one of the family. “He’d let himself into the house and put the kettle on,” recalls Brown.

Industry observers note that even adversaries were entertained, such as Ron Dixon. The colourful one-time owner of Dundee actually bought Brown’s family home in St Madoes for those rare times when he was in Scotland. The Canadian complained to the St Johnstone owner that he’d been sold a pup when buying the Dens Park club. “They told me I was getting a sleeping giant!” he lamented. Brown told Sturrock. “Aye, they’re all lying in the cemetery!” the former Dundee United winger replied.

Memo to Dundonians of either hue: Brown has a few arch things to say about Dundee natives. However, citizens of the fair city of Perth will enjoy Brown’s book, likewise anyone partial to a classic rags-to-riches tale.

Building My Life: The Geoff Brown Story will be launched in the Centenary Suite at McDiarmid Park on November 30, from 6pm until 8pm. The book will be available in the St Johnstone club shop in Perth City Centre and at McDiarmid Park on match days.

Tech Report: THE BREAKDOWN: The real reasons why Enzo Maresca's Man City can't stop losing - from anonymous Enzo Fernandez abandoning Elliot Anderson, to the fatal flaws in Italian's set-up that are being brutally exposed

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1738 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 05:23 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • It has been revealed that diet Pep is losing his fizz.
  • Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a upcoming manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 05:23 EST, 26 November 2026.

It has been revealed that diet Pep is losing his fizz. Enzo Maresca may look like Pep Guardiola, may have learned his craft under his Manchester City predecessor, but his quest to follow in his mentor’s footsteps has all gone a bit flat.

Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a upcoming manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.

Three months in, and three defeats on the spin that left them six points behind Arsenal have made it clear that something is not clicking for Maresca.

Recent findings suggest that is the uncertainty around the potential punishment following that guilty verdict taking its toll? Is Maresca just suffering from his usual late autumn dips? He suffered similar tricky periods around late October and early November at Leicester and his first season at Chelsea too.

Or is there something at the heart of his side, of his system, that’s finally being exposed?

Enzo Maresca's Man City have slumped to three straight Premier League defeats after a promising start to the season.

In a recent development, guardiola’s City was all about control. Keep the ball, dominate the pitch, play the game at your pace, on your terms.

Maresca’s City, regardless of how well they started the season, has been about anything but. It has been about triumph amid chaos, about moments of magic more than the overarching method.

Without that control, City’s defensive complications have been laid bare. The 13 goals they have let in after 10 games is their most at this stage since 2008. They haven’t kept a clean sheet in their last eight matches in all competitions. That's a drought longer than at any point under Guardiola.

Their biggest problem over City's three successive Premier League defeats is just how susceptible they have been to counter attacks.

Only Newcastle have faced more shots this season following ‘fast breaks’ – data giants Opta's term for counter attacks – than City’s 17, and 11 of those have come in the last three games: six against Nottingham Forest, two of which led to goals, three against Brighton and another two against Aston Villa.

According to recent reports, maresca’s side are being more profligate in possession, too. Over the first seven games of the season, they lost the ball 120 times a game on average – one of the best figures in the division. Since then, it’s closer to 140.

City have been wasteful in possession and regularly overrun on the counter, with Elliot Anderson (centre) too often left isolated in midfield.

ANDERSON CAN'T DO IT ALL ON HIS OWN.

Recent findings suggest that many of these problems have their roots in Maresca's serious problems in midfield. Rodri, the best holding midfielder of his generation, was always going to be hard to replace but Maresca appears to be expecting Elliot Anderson to do it all on his own.

It has been revealed that anderson is at his best when he’s free to get up and down the pitch, box to box, using his physicality not just in winning the ball back but progressing it. No midfielder played more passes into the final third last season than Anderson at Forest. At one stage of the campaign, he had played more progressive passes than any other player across Europe’s top five leagues.

And yet Maresca is forcing Anderson to play as the sitter while his golden boy Enzo Fernandez, whom he pushed City to sign in the summer for £125million, is roaming free and high up the pitch.

Maresca likes his teams to build up in a 3-1-6 shape, which sees Fernandez push up as an extra attacking midfielder, and leaves Anderson manning the fort alone.

When City lose the ball, though, it leaves them wide open.

Recent findings suggest that this is the opening goal City conceded against Forest. Josko Gvardiol wants to play the ball inside but has only red shirts and empty green space ahead of him. Anderson is the only man free, but even he is too high and has a Forest player ready to cut off the pass. Eventually, Gvardiol gets robbed and Forest score.

According to recent reports, A lack of options for Josko Gvardiol (left) led to Forest's opener against City. Enzo Fernandez (circled) was caught high up the pitch, way ahead of the deeper Anderson (also circled).

Here’s another moment in the defeat by Brighton.

The Seagulls break forward on the flank and Anderson races over to close the ball down. Fernandez is, you guessed it, high up the pitch.

City have no midfield cover to stop the ball inside, Abdukodir Khusanov gets drawn in and leaves loads of space in behind for Yasin Ayari to exploit and cross to Maxim De Cuyper for a great chance.

The lack of protection offered by Anderson and especially the more advanced Fernandez was again on show against Brighton, who were able to exploit the acres of space left in midfield.

Recent findings suggest that fernandez is doing what Maresca wants, but it’s not working. Maresca needs more from him, especially when Anderson’s instincts are to press and harass and bully, which can leave gaps when he does not yet read the game as comprehensively as Rodri.

Anderson sits in the top five for ball recoveries among midfielders to have played 500 minutes this season. Fernandez is in the bottom five. That figure becomes even more alarming when you consider Anderson has created more chances from open play than Fernandez, too.

Ayyoub Bouaddi showed at the World Cup that he had the most similar profile to Rodri. It might be time for Maresca to put some faith in him.

Sources indicate that maresca has always wanted his goalkeeper to be an 11th outfielder. In his one season at Leicester, Mads Hermansen played more passes than any goalkeeper in Championship history. During his time at Chelsea, there was a shaky moment in a draw with Arsenal when loud groans greeted a misplaced pass from Robert Sanchez.

‘I am the guy who asks Robert to do that,’ said Maresca after that game. ‘The moment he stops doing that, he is not going to play.’.

Donnarumma, though, for all his (usually) excellent shot-stopping, is anything but a ball-playing goalkeeper. The ball rolled under his foot from a simple back pass against Coventry and so nearly crept over the line. He gifted France an early lead while on international duty with Italy when he passed the ball straight to Michael Olise.

Only two keepers made more errors leading to shots than Donnarumma across the course of last season, with many of those being with his feet, like when he gifted Kai Havertz an equaliser in City's victory over Arsenal in April.

Gianluigi Donnarumma has never been good with his feet - now his excellent shot-stopping has taken a dip too.

The Italian should have easily dealt with Nicolas Jackson's second goal in City's 2-1 loss at Aston Villa.

The decision to let James Trafford leave in the summer, especially with Guardiola’s impending departure and a manager like Maresca coming in, is looking ever more misguided.

Recent findings suggest that trafford is not immune to mistakes either, of course. He erred badly when trying to play out from the back for City against Spurs last season and made an almost identical howler for Leeds at Bournemouth in October. But he is still far more confident at playing out from the back than Donnarumma.

The double blow for Maresca is that the trade-off with Donnarumma – where he makes up for his weakness with the ball at his feet by making saves that other keepers can’t make – is no longer paying off either.

Nicolas Jackson’s shot squirmed straight through him to hand Villa victory and condemn City to their first defeat of the season.

When you are coughing up chances as frequently as City are, Maresca needs his keeper to be on top form.

Do you know who is keeping the ball out of his net? James Trafford. He boasts the highest save percentage of any goalkeeper in the top flight, keeping out 81 per cent of the shots on target coming his way. Donnarumma is 15th, on less than 66 per cent.

According to Opta’s expected data, Trafford has also prevented more than four goals that he should have conceded from the quality of the shots he’s faced. Again, he’s the best in the Premier League. Donnarumma is middle of the pack.

Industry observers note that ‘At the moment, I’m not thinking about the goalkeeping situation,’ mentioned Maresca recently. Without Trafford there and just 34-year-old Geronimo Rulli as back-up, he doesn’t really have a choice but to persist with Donnarumma and hope he improves.

When the goals stop flowing for Erling Haaland, City can't mask all their other problems.

So used are we now to seeing the Norwegian on the scoresheet, having notched nine in City’s opening eight matches, that when he goes just two games without a goal it feels as if he’s on a barren spell.

The issue, though, is less down to Haaland and more that City’s build-up in recent weeks is struggling to get him into the game.

In a recent development, city are finding it more difficult to get Haaland on the ball. His touches per game are falling steadily but, crucially, so are the quality of the chances his team-mates are creating for him.

Haaland had more than one Opta-defined 'major chance' in five of City’s opening seven games. He’s had just one come his way in each of their three defeats.

According to recent reports, his expected goals (xG) tally is dropping too. Across City’s winning streak, Haaland’s average xG per match was 0.81. Only once, against Liverpool, did it drop below 0.5.

Over the three defeats, it’s just 0.45 and has not once gone above 0.5.

Antoine Semenyo missing the last three games through injury has not helped, especially when teams now try to pack the middle of the pitch and force City wide.

Haaland will come good, he always does, but City need to start serving him again if Maresca wants to get through this tricky spell and stop the vultures from circling.

The Japan international is recovering from a hamstring injury which required surgery and has kept him out since May.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Mitoma, 29, last featured for the Seagulls in the 3-0 Premier League victory over Wolves on May 9, when he was forced off after 58 minutes.

He has since missed Brighton's final two league matches of last season and all 11 Premier League fixtures so far this campaign.

Hürzeler confirmed the winger would not be available against Newcastle but suggested he was approaching an important milestone in his rehabilitation.

"Kaoru won't be available. That's what I can say. But I'm quite positive that all the other players will be available," remarked the Brighton boss.

"Like I said a few weeks ago, we have to be patient with him. He's getting really close, so I think in the next one or two weeks he'll be back training with the team. That's very positive.".

Mitoma does though face a battle to get back in the first team. Maxim De Cuyper has impressed during his absence, while Femi Azeez, Ibrahin Osman, Diego Gomez and Yankuba Minteh can all operate on the left flank.

Ibraham is pushing for more Premier League minutes after his two goal blast against Craiova in the Conference League last night.

“Yeah, I think he [Osman] showed a really good performance [against Craiova], he scored the first goal, he created plenty of other moments.

“We know that his biggest quality is one against one, especially against teams who are sitting in a low block, this is very helpful to have these one against one players.

“He highlighted a very impressive style today, besides that I'm really happy that he understands more and more how key it is to keep working hard for having the clean sheet and also he's responsible for that.

“As an offensive player because that's always the foundation of our game.”.

In the hearts and minds of AC Milan fans around the world, Pippo Inzaghi’s name is inseparably linked to Athens.

Industry observers note that inzaghi gave Milan their seventh Champions League title on 23 May 2007 in the Greek capital with a brace that swept Liverpool aside. The first goal was an Andrea Pirlo free-kick that he deflected in, the second an assist from Kaka that he rounded Pepe Reina from and slotted in.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, it was he who allowed the Rossoneri to take their long-awaited and long-desired revenge on the Reds after the Istanbul defeat two years earlier. That feat – at the Spyros Louis Olympic Stadium and not at the Georgios Karaiskakis Stadium – has remained in the minds of all Milan fans.

It is the most recent of the Champions League titles raised to the sky, and while Inzaghi’s mind is on finishing the job with Palermo (top of Serie B), he will watch his old side on TV tonight. The former striker spoke to La Gazzetta dello Sport.

Dor you and for Milan, thinking back to Athens is never trivial….

According to recent reports, “Absolutely. In Athens I experienced one of the most vital nights of my career, so it’s a city I associate with special memories and that’s why it will always remain close to my heart.”.

Recent findings suggest that tell us three memories from that game. Let’s start with a pre-match one….

“The anticipation of the match: I knew how notable that final was and I felt it could be a special evening.”.

Recent findings suggest that “The highlight was, of course, the second goal. A moment later, I realised the cup was really close.”.

And one after the final whistle….

“After that final, I didn’t sleep for ten days. I woke up in the middle of the night thinking that victory with my goals had been a dream.”.

Given what that cup represented, that is, the famous ‘after Istanbul, there’s always Athens’ that was printed on the back of AC Milan’s second shirt this season, is the 2006-07 Champions League a joy comparable to Italy’s World Cup victory in Berlin a few months earlier?

“They’re two different memories because they’ve both enriched my footballing life. Winning the World Cup is the ultimate accolade for any footballer.

“Athens, however, also had a special meaning for Milan’s history: we were coming off a disappointment that I’d experienced from the outside, from the stands [he was injured] and I could finally be on the pitch to contribute to the victory.

“Fate gave me a second chance, and it went as you all know… However, I wouldn’t rank the two nights of glory because I carry them with me in different ways.”.

Before Milan-Atalanta, when you came to San Siro, you understood from the huge applause and chants how much the Rossoneri fans still love you and you mentioned: “Every time I come back here it’s like it’s the first time.”.

“Returning to San Siro and feeling that affection was truly emotional for me, especially because it was the first time for my son Edoardo, who is now five years old.”.

What does it mean to you, years after leaving AC Milan as a player and the 2014-15 season in which you were the coach, to still be so loved by the fans?

According to recent reports, “I spent extraordinary years at Milan: the bond with the fans was born from goals, victories, but also from the commitment I always tried to put in. Knowing that all this has gone down in history is a priceless gift.”.

What do you hope for Milan on their return to Athens tonight, needing a win given their position in the Europa League table?

“I hope we can face the match with character and return home having experienced a great European night. I know how much that shirt means and how much the fans expect from a match like this. I hope the team can give them joy and a victory.”.

Sources indicate that just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

In a recent development, it felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

Their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

This is a team who can stir the blood, surf the emotion and triumph against the odds more than any other; who have a proud history of doing so. Who feel the injustice at its most acute and could feed off that.

Recent findings suggest that in the end Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the season. Their first under Andoni Iraola. And comprehensively so. It could not have come at a worse time for them and for the Premier League, and for the fans of every other club who wanted to see City humbled. On the pitch.

Industry observers note that there was another sense of injustice. Up until the dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch, Liverpool were the better side. Especially as they attacked the Kop in the second half, drawing saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma, and began to build the kind of momentum that has, over the years, appeared to suck the ball into the net.

Industry observers note that this is not a slight on Iraola, but it is hard to imagine Jürgen Klopp not riding that wave of emotion more effectively and wringing more out of the available players. Turning to the fans; imploring them; cajoling them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 27 Nov 2026 06:53.

Rayan Cherki made a strong impression on Jeffinho during their time together at Olympique Lyonnais in 2023. Appearing as a guest on the Charla Podcast, the Brazilian forward first praised the technical qualities of the current Manchester City player, before describing a much more divisive character.

'Rayan Cherki. What a player! He is a bit annoying, but he strikes the ball and drives it with both feet. He is very strong' - he explained.

It has been revealed that jeffinho then went on to explain what could bother him about the Frenchman. 'You can see it in the way he plays. He dribbles and looks at the others' - the Brazilian noted, naming Bradley Barcola among the best players he has played alongside and liked.

The testimony becomes even more interesting when he discusses relationships within the Lyon dressing room.

According to Jeffinho, Cherki belonged to a fairly closed group that also included Corentin Tolisso, Alexandre Lacazette and Anthony Lopes. The Brazilian describes a 'small clique' of important players who stayed together a lot and, in his view, had real influence in the team.

At the time, Lyon's management had nevertheless denied the existence of a 'Lyonnais gang'.

Asked about the player with the most assertive temperament in this circle, Jeffinho naturally named Cherki.

In a recent development, he explained that the group 'weighed a little on the team', while not hiding that their attitude could sometimes annoy him. His testimony remains nuanced, however: with each criticism of the Frenchman's behaviour, the former Lyon player returns to his immense quality as a player.

It has been revealed that jeffinho also extended his judgement to Cherki's current situation at Manchester City. 'Cherki plays extremely well, but you also have to respect the others' - he said, before suggesting that his attitude could sometimes have a negative impact on his team.

A very personal view of the attacking midfielder, but one that above all sheds light on the relationships he observed in the Lyon dressing room.

Both are in their second spells at the club and the former had his best year at Oakwell during the German's memorable first season as head coach in 2018-19.

Given what the Reds are currently experiencing, that magnificent promotion campaign must seem like a world away.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The pair are now fighting fires at the wrong end of League One; beleaguered Barnsley currently prop up the table following a wretched 11-match winless streak.

In his second coming at Oakwell, Stendel named McGeehan, a player he rates and trusts, as his on-pitch leader in the summer.

So far this term, the Reds chief has largely been spared the ire of increasingly agitated followers; most have elected to vent their frustration toward the Oakwell hierarchy instead.

But given Barnsley's atrocious autumnal numbers - two points taken from the last available 33 - chatter is also starting to centre on the German's position.

For McGeehan, the club's top-scorer with nine goals, it provides a personal element in his quest to help the stricken Reds change the narrative of a hard season.

He also shares sympathy with Stendel, given Barnsley's tendencies to continually shoot themselves in the foot - which he feels has nothing to do with the head coach.

A case in point was at Bradford City on Tuesday, when all three of the visitors' concessions were self-inflicted.

Speaking ahead of the crunch trip to fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon, McGeehan remarked: "I think coming in after the game, a lot of the boys were saying: 'the gaffer's going to be pulling his hair out' because that was just down to the players' mistakes.

"And it's happened too many times this season, we've made poor individual errors that have led to goals and caused us to lose games we probably shouldn't have.

"We want to get a positive result for everyone at the club.

It has been revealed that "But obviously the gaffer's someone I've worked with before and you can see it completely consumes him. He wants the very best and he's passionate to get Barnsley into a good place, as we all are. We're all fighting together.

According to recent reports, "It can all change very swiftly. But it starts with us on the pitch getting a positive result. This poor run's lasted way too long and we've got to draw a line in the sand.

"Obviously, there's a lot of positive things that we've done in games and it's just trying to get that game where it clicks and then you go from there.".

The busy run to the turn of the year looks critical for Barnsley, presently four points adrift of safety, with several fixtures coming up against sides around them.

Should the Reds manage to chip away with some much-needed wins, January will come into sharp focus.

Recruiting a defensive lieutenant and an experienced leader of the line are surely two huge priorities for a side that is right now dangerously weak in both boxes, where games are decided, despite getting other things right elsewhere.

On the importance of bringing in some seniority in the upcoming year at the sharp ends of the pitch, McGeehan observed: "Potentially. You can look at that obviously when you're not doing well, you sort of start to pick apart different things.

"At the start of the season, when we started quite well, you sort of think: 'oh, we've got a youthful, energetic side'.

In a recent development, "There's always two ways you can spin it. I've seen experienced players make mistakes for goals and be short of confidence as well. January will come and teams always make signings but all we are concentrating on is now and do what we can with what we've got.

Industry observers note that "We've got some really good players here and hopefully we can turn the corner. It's everyone sticking together and trying to fight. It's the only way out of this.".

McGeehan admits that listening to opposing managers and pundits continuing to label Barnsley as a good footballing side is becoming 'boring'.

For his part, Stendel concurs, adding: "This is easy to say when you win the game and keep the points. I don't like it.".

The Reds boss also has no truck with the disquiet of supporters either.

It spilled over at the final whistle at Valley Parade on Tuesday with chants of 'You're not fit to wear the shirt' aimed at players.

Sources indicate that the Oakwell boss, who confirmed that Reyes Cleary is not yet back in training, with Cieran Slicker and Makenzie Kirk having problems ahead of the weekend, added: "When you are upset, you say things like that. This is not different at Barnsley to other clubs in the world.

"I also have to support and protect my team. They are trying to do their best. It is not enough at the moment for the expectation of what we have as a club and also not for the supporters.".

The former Huddersfield Town, Swansea City and Barnsley chief had been at the helm for almost a year after replacing Michael Dodds last September.

He pulled the Chairboys away from trouble at the wrong end of the League One table with the Buckinghamshire club finishing in the top half by the end of 2025-26.

Duff, who was appointed by the Bantams just shy of a month after leaving Adams Park, said: "It's a good club with a lot of investment off the pitch and they spent a lot of money on the pitch. There's some good people there.

According to recent reports, "I don't carry around the bitterness and all things like that. Part of the job is they wanted to change the manager and they did it.

Industry observers note that "I wouldn't be here (otherwise). It is what it is.

"It was a pretty good year, I think we would have been fifth in the league in the period of time I was (there). But obviously, it wasn't deemed good enough, so you move on.".

Duff, who has lost just once in his opening 10 matches in charge at City, indicates captain Antoni Sarcevic is 'touch and go' ahead of the trip south.

Sarcevic missed the victory over Barnsley after picking up a knock in last weekend’s draw against Doncaster Rovers.

City have potential issues in midfield, with loanee Kieran Morgan absent for the foreseeable future after breaking his foot on Tuesday.

George Lapslie returned to full training after a hamstring issue on Wednesday, but Duff claims he will be guided by the club's medical staff ahead of deciding whether to involve him or Sarcevic this weekend - amid the club's hectic forthcoming schedule.

The City chief has confirmed that adding to his options in the middle of the park is an area where the club are looking to strengthen in January.

By Lewis Blain | 27 Nov 2026 07:15.

Liverpool have received encouraging news regarding Víctor Munoz after the winger suffered a worrying knee injury against Club Brugge on Wednesday evening.

The Spanish winger was forced off following a heavy collision during the first half of the 3-0 win, with the initial images raising fears of a potentially serious problem.

However, early tests have reportedly suggested that the injury is not as bad as first feared, offering Reds boss Andoni Iraola some welcome relief ahead of the Merseyside Derby on Sunday afternoon.

Munoz suffered the injury after his knee became caught during a strong collision with a Brugge player inside the opposition penalty area.

According to recent reports, the incident prompted immediate concern among his teammates, with a stretcher brought onto the pitch to assist the winger. However, he eventually managed to leave the field under his own steam, accompanied by Dominik Szoboszlai.

It initially appeared particularly concerning, but subsequent tests have provided a more positive indication of the extent of the damage.

According to recent reports, according to reports from Spain, the initial assessment suggests that Munoz has suffered a 'severe' blow to his knee rather than a serious injury. Definitive confirmation is still pending, but the early indications are encouraging.

Iraola also offered a cautiously optimistic assessment after the match.

Recent findings suggest that "He felt a lot of pain at the moment, but by the end of the match he was feeling better. I hope it's nothing notable," the Liverpool coach said.

Although it remains unclear whether Munoz will be fit for this weekend's Merseyside derby, the initial diagnosis is certainly reassuring for Iraola.

The severity of the collision and the sight of the stretcher initially suggested that Liverpool could be facing a significant injury setback, potentially ruling the winger out for an extended period.

Instead, the early tests indicate that the problem may be limited to a heavy blow, although the club will understandably wait for definitive confirmation before making any decisions on his availability.

With a major fixture approaching, Muñoz's potential involvement would be a welcome boost, but avoiding a serious injury is the most important outcome at this stage.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a difficult summer transfer window, the Blades are one point outside the Championship play-off places are 17 matches.

Whilst the players will always deserve the lion's share of the credit for that, with manager Wilder next in the queue, he pointed to the large number of people working hard behind the scenes in largely unheralded roles.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"Now with Wyescout and all the other sources that we can get individually on players, unit meetings on individual players to give the players an idea of what they're coming up against, gameplan, so much work goes in from the staff, the coaches, myself, analysing it, seeing what little areas that we can find an advantage, looking at strengths and weaknesses as always," he said.

"With tree-game weeks as well, it's an incredible amount of work on every front, putting together training sessions, loading on the players what they need to do, what they don't need to do, when we need to come off and when we need to stick it on them.

"For players that are not starting, what they need to do as well, you know.

"The amount of work that the analysts do in flagging stuff up and then we're all trying to put it together and put a gameplan together to give us the best opportunity.

"It's not me at 10 o'clock asking, 'Boys, what happened last night?' and let's go and put the nets up and get on with it attitude.

"A lot of work goes into it, but when you do get it right, whether it's over the season or whether it's just that chasing that winning feeling that we talk about on a Saturday night, it all feels worthwhile.".

The Blades have scored the most (nine) and conceded the fewest (one) goals from set pieces in this season's Championship.

"It's an attitude from the players," remarked Wilder. "It's a review, a best practise. A lot of work goes into it away from the lights – unit meetings, set-piece meetings, all stuff that's at every club and has been a massive part of the game for a long time.

"We want to be the best in every department – creating chances, keeping clean sheets, set plays, running stats, physical stats.

"We've got good delivery, we've got players that want to go and attack it.".

Meanwhile, Wilder believes Jordan Ayew has “found a home” at Bramall Lane after finding himself unemployed when the summer transfer window shut.

The 35-year-old was released when Leicester City were relegated last season but is starting to flourish after being picked up by the Blades, as shown by his brilliant assist for Sydie Peck's equaliser against Southampton on Tuesday.

“He’s a signing that we made and one that was well talked about,” mentioned Wilder.

In a recent development, “He’s been outstanding for us. He’s linked the play up, dropped in and got hold of the ball, played in the pockets, created chances and then set Sydie up for his equaliser.

"There was a lot of noise when he signed, as there has been for quite a lot of things that have happened at the start.

Recent findings suggest that “All we have to do is get our heads down, and all Jordan has to do is go and play in the way that he has done. I think he's found a home; I'm sure he has. He really enjoys playing for us and I'm enjoying managing and coaching him.”.

In a recent development, having lost three of four in the UEL thus far, Milan are currently outside even the top 24 places, so they must secure the majority of the remaining 12 points on offer to climb. Their hosts tonight have started much better and are inside the top eight, with 10 points on the board.

Amorim will go with a strong side, or the best possible at least with the injury situation. Pietro Terracciano, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Luka Modric, Samuel Chukwueze, Strahinja Pavlovic, Davide Bartesaghi, Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Francesco Camarda are all out.

Sources indicate that we start with a duel on Milan’s right flank between Diego Moreira and Bruno Onyemaechi. For the Nigerian defender, it will be just his seventh start of the season (out of 15 games played) and this might be arguably his toughest test yet.

Moreira meanwhile has been outstanding in Serie A, with four goals and four assists to his name already. Yet, he hasn’t really got going in Europe yet just like the whole team, given he doesn’t have a goal contribution outside of domestic action. Tonight is a chance to get the ball rolling.

It has been revealed that the main threat for Olympiacos is without doubt the attacking midfielder Jota Silva. The former Besiktas man is already on six goals from his 14 appearances (plus one assist) and has really made the No.10 role his. That noted, he too is without a goal or assist in Europe so far.

Meanwhile, this is a huge opportunity for Ardon Jashari, as he admitted in his pre-match press conference. The Swiss did very well off the bench against Frosinone and Modric’s injury has opened up a spot for him to take the reins this evening, though he has not always delivered so far when given that task.

Moving back to Milan’s attack, a significant night awaits for Goncalo Ramos. He scored in the 4-0 rout of RB Salzburg but is dry in Europe aside from that. The Portuguese ended a one-month goal drought on Sunday by scoring against Frosinone in a move he started and finished, which offers encouragement after a difficult start in red and black.

His opponent will be someone who knows Milan very well, but from the other side of the city. Lorenzo Pirola spent several years in Inter’s academy and has found himself in Athens as one of the leaders of the Olympiacos defence. Tonight will carry a bit of extra meaning, especially amid talk of a potential call-up from Roberto Mancini.

Recent findings suggest that 🇵🇹 #Ramos ends his drought! Will a goal like this unlock the #ACMilan striker? 🔓.

🎧 Latest podcast: https://t.co/QfaRwdNXza pic.twitter.com/nafNdAUzuL.

— SempreMilanTV (@SempreMilanTV) November 25, 2026.

Armando Gonzalez is the one who will lead the line for the home side at the Karaiskakis Stadium. The 23-year-old Mexican has scored once so far in the Europa League, but he has three goals overall in four starts and is vying for that starting No.9 position.

Koni De Winter was solid in Sunday’s win meanwhile, and yet he is in need of a performance having really struggled in his battle with Lenny Joseph in the defeat to Ferencvaros last month. The Haitian international – not even their normal starting striker – constantly got the better of the Belgian, who has been up and down in recent weeks.

Finally, we end with the contest between two midfield veterans: Remo Freuler and Adrien Rabiot. The latter has become the anchor of the Erythrolefkoi midfield, and he knows the Rossoneri very well having played for many years in Serie A. The 34-year-old Swiss international also has four assists from a deep-lying playmaker role.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, it has been a tale of two competitions for Rabiot, just like Moreira. The Frenchman has tallied 5 goals and 6 assists in Serie A, but only one assist in European play, and he actually drew criticism after his performances against Bournemouth and Ferencvaros. It is time to bring that league form onto the continent.

Tech Report: Silly Leeds United punishment indicates Daniel Farke's serious approach to complacency

  • Earlier in the season, the German manager told The Yorkshire Post of his – slightly tongue in cheek – horror at Ao Tanaka wearing gloves in training before the weather had turned cold, and this week he gave a member of staff a dressing down to try and keep his squad grounded after Saturday's hugely impressive 4-1 win at Chelsea.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Earlier in the season, the German manager told The Yorkshire Post of his – slightly tongue in cheek – horror at Ao Tanaka wearing gloves in training before the weather had turned cold, and this week he gave a member of staff a dressing down to try and keep his squad grounded after Saturday's hugely impressive 4-1 win at Chelsea.

Both the "crime" and the punishment were light-hearted but with a serious message about complacency, and it is a balance Farke always looks to strike.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Leeds are in seventh in the Premier League and have consistently been around the likely positions to qualify for Europe this season, but Farke has always taken a two-pronged attitude towards expectations, encouraging supporters to get ahead of themselves but not those who work for him.

"What I can guarantee is I will make sure that no one here at the training ground at Thorp Arch is too major time and I'm not one per cent concerned about my players," he stated when the topic of Europe was raised ahead of Saturday's Premier League visit from newly-promoted Coventry City.

"We had a staff member this week who came out after a great win against Chelsea more or less celebrating in the first session.

"I know it's a bit colder right now and you have to put yourself into warm clothes but instead of wearing a hat (for training) – a hat is totally fine – he was wearing a snood over his head like a 20-year-old creative No 10 who enjoys himself.

"It was as if he had won the game at Chelsea all alone.

In a recent development, "It was a long working day for him, I made sure. He was treating our kit men and from now on he stays in shorts and T-shirts until the end of January on the outside pitches.

"I don't allow anyone to be substantial time, not one staff member, not one player. We know exactly what we're coming from and if anyone thinks we are too good for this and can be cool like a 20-year-old No 10, one of my staff members, I will make sure that everyone is back to work and doesn't enjoy himself too much.

"We have not achieved 38 points so far (his mark for avoiding relegation), so there's no reason to lean back, just enjoy and stop working.

It has been revealed that "It's good to be already on 17 points at this stage (11 games in). It's definitely a good amount and gives us confidence and belief in what you're doing.

"But at this level the momentum can change quickly and for that we won't allow ourselves to be too big time or to enjoy ourselves too much.

"We are in a good mood at the moment and we work, train and play with confidence but nothing else.

Sources indicate that "The Premier League is the best league in the world. We can only win points if we are 100 per cent on it.".

A silly response to a seemingly trivial offence (with a much more serious underlying issue) is a balance Farke is conscious of striking.

"It's perhaps not typical for a German fella to have a good sense of humour – at least that's a bit the reputation – but I think in general everyone is at his best in every job when you feel valued, when you feel comfortable when you do your job with confidence and this is also what we try to create," commented Farke.

Sources indicate that "I've seen some statistics that we were the hardest-working side over the last (Premier League) weekend. At Chelsea we covered more distance and high-speed intensity runs than any other team at Premier League level.

"This is one side of how we work really hard with focused, concentrated work but we always want to do this with a smile on our face.

"We want to make sure that everyone enjoys coming to work and it's not just hoping for the next day off so I don't see the manager, the staff member or assistant coach.

"Sometimes you have to give them a day off but we also want to create an atmosphere where everyone feels safe and is allowed to make a joke and also joke at my costs.

"You also give the sign that you know how notable and how serious football is but it's never more important than the human being.

Industry observers note that "When I name the squad on Friday there are some tough decisions and top players won't make it. When I name the starting line-up it's tough for them but then we have to make sure that we have something to cheer and to laugh about.

"Hopefully the most vital thing is success and winning points but also to have a good atmosphere.

"I hope my jokes are not too old-school for the players because I'm getting older and older.".

Meanwhile, striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a upcoming contract until the end of 2028-29, by when he will have just turned 32.

Sources indicate that "I want to keep my best players without giving them the scenario that they can lean back because they've signed a ten-year deal," said his manager. "I've made it clear (to the board) but it was easy because everyone in our hierarchy wants to keep the best players.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 27 Nov 2026 07:31.

Tottenham Hotspur have suffered another injury setback, with Savio expected to miss several weeks after sustaining a hamstring problem against Ipswich Town.

The Brazilian winger had only recently returned from a previous muscle injury before being forced off during last weekend's 2-0 victory in the Premier League.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi now faces the prospect of being without the winger for a significant period during a busy end to 2026.

Savio made his first appearance since the 1-1 draw with Manchester United on October 10th when he came off the bench against the Tractor Boys.

However, his return lasted only around 20 minutes, with the 22-year-old going down inside the opposition penalty area after an impressive run before being helped from the pitch by Tottenham's medical staff.

According to recent reports, his exact recovery timeline has not yet been determined, but The Athletic report that he is now expected to miss several weeks. One source has even stated Savio could miss all seven of Tottenham's remaining matches in 2026.

De Zerbi confirmed that the winger had suffered a recurrence of the same muscle injury, expressing his frustration at losing an vital member of his squad.

In a recent development, "I'm very angry about that, because Savio is a crucial player for us," the Spurs boss noted. "It's the same injury, and it is the worst thing from today.".

Savio has endured a difficult start to life in north London following his summer move from Manchester City in a deal worth up to £85m. Despite scoring on his debut against Charlton Athletic, he has managed just seven appearances due to fitness problems.

Tottenham already have significant attacking concerns, with Savio joining Mathys Tel, Mykhailo Mudryk, Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert on the injury list.

The north London outfit were already expected to explore the market for a upcoming striker, but De Zerbi may now need to consider a more versatile forward capable of operating centrally and out wide.

That would help address the lack of options on the left flank, although Savio's absence could also create opportunities for academy graduate Luca Williams-Barnett.

The 18-year-old gem scored and assisted on his first Premier League start against Ipswich, offering De Zerbi an encouraging alternative.

However, with several attacking players unavailable and Savio potentially missing the remainder of the year, adding another forward in January would make sense.

Spurs need greater depth across their frontline, and a versatile signing could help address more than one problem at once.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Minstermen, who ended their 10-year exile from the Football League last season, sit fifth ahead of Saturday's trip to Colchester United, raising hopes of successive promotions.

Lindsey is embracing that pressure at a club that have made no secret of their ambition to go back-to-back.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sources indicate that "The only pressure I've got is from myself because I know what this group is capable of," stated the York boss. "I put pressure on myself to do well and believe that we're good enough to have a really good season.

"I haven't got any pressure from anywhere else. It's a football club that want to get somewhere really swiftly, which suits me as well.

According to recent reports, "I'm ambitious. I don't want to just make the numbers up and finish mid-table. It would be a bit of a waste of a season, even though that would be seen as success to a lot of people.

"It's our first season in the division for 10 years and I want to do really well.".

York have lost just four of their 16 games, bouncing back from consecutive defeats to claim their first win on the road at Rochdale before sharing the spoils with fellow promotion hopefuls Walsall.

City also have an FA Cup tie against Carlisle to look forward to for a place in the third round.

"I think we're in a really good position in the division," added Lindsey.

"The football club hasn't been in this league for 10 years. To say we are where we are in the division and into the second round of the FA Cup, I see that as a massive positive.

"I'm over the moon with the start that we've had.".

Rather than making wholesale changes when he arrived in the summer, Lindsey has sought to build on the winning culture he inherited.

Maintaining the momentum generated in the National League was an important consideration as York made the step up to League Two, with the newly introduced manager recognising the value of what was already in place.

"Definitely," said Lindsey, whose side are just one point adrift of the automatic promotion places.

Industry observers note that "The club before I turned up was a winning machine anyway, which is why I didn't change loads straight away. I didn't feel I had to because I thought there was a lot of good work done here.

"I just wanted to put my stamp on it, which I feel I've done, and the lads have taken on that information and executed it brilliantly.

"It's a strange situation because when you come into a club as a manager, you're normally coming into a bit of a mess. But I wasn't; I was coming into a real structured team who were used to winning. I had to sit into that.

"My style isn't too dissimilar to what was happening before. There are little tweaks where I feel I've made us a little bit more robust for this division. Over the years of me being here, it'll be more my team.".

The recalled forward, who started ahead of Bojan Radulovic, was excellent in the first half-hour at the Club Doncaster Sports Village and provided assists for the visitors' two goals from captain Cameron Humphreys and top-scorer Joe Taylor.

After the game changed following Bali Mumba's 34th-minute dismissal, Fletcher dropped to the left to help the team cope with playing with a man light.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The frontman continued to perform responsibly for the team before being sacrificed on 55 minutes when another midfielder in Marcus Harness entered the fray.

But Fletcher's impact was not lost upon Drury, whose side draw level on points with leaders Stockport County and maintained their fine away record this term - while recording their first-ever league victory, at the fifth attempt, at this South Yorkshire venue.

Drury, whose side return to action at home to Stevenage on Tuesday, stated: "I thought he started the game so well.

"At half-time, we could have taken somebody off and changed the shape and everything, but we noted we wanted to leave it for five minutes to see where it is.

"People understood the roles and Ashley Fletcher within that, I thought he was excellent.

It has been revealed that "I was gutted for him that he had to come off, but he's a humble guy and he recognises the necessity of it. Hopefully, next time we have a game, he'll be more involved in that.".

Despite playing with 10 men for around an hour, Town's organisation reminded spot on, allied to their sense of control and maintenance of an attacking threat.

Industry observers note that drury added: "That was probably the most pleasing aspect of it. You can't stop them putting you low, you can't stop them getting to your box because you've got one less player.

In a recent development, "But you can hold the line as high as you can and I felt we did that. We were aggressive with it.

"When we were put low, we were fighting to stop crosses. We were picking up in the box. Listen, we had some hairy moments in there, of course, but I think sometimes you get what you deserve and I felt the players deserved that result.

"I really did, particularly going down to 10 men for the amount of time that we did.".

#165013. Breaking: Structural basis of RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CAST systems
