It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline says. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”.

Recent findings suggest that good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

It has been revealed that today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

It has been revealed that frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

"It's a substantial blow for us," said Jakirovic of Iroegbunam's injury, picked up against Brighton and Hove Albion Sunday.

"This is what I'm telling them all the time - that you have to be ready and work very hard in every training session so when the opportunity comes, you are ready.

Like Dominic Calvert-Lewin on Thursday, and Brenden Aaronson in August, the Japan midfielder has singed up until the end of the 2028-29 campaign.

It continues the very sensible pattern of trying to tie down key players at the same time as making some of the most expensive signings in the club's history as the Whites look to kick on in their second season in the Premier League.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Tanaka joined Leeds in the Championship from second-tier German side Fortuna Dusseldorf in 2024.

The 28-year-old is very much a confidence player and despite having played at the World Cup for his country and although he was a key part of the Leeds team that won the title in his debut season, last term was his first playing top-tier European football, and it seemed to take him a while to believe he belonged there.

With the Whites adopted a more direct style to make the step up, the cultured midfielder's 28 appearances were split equally between starts and cameos from the bench.

But since appearing as a half-time substitute against Brentford in the first home Premier League games of this season, he has started every match. His fresh deal is just another indication to him of his importance to manager Daniel Farke.

It was Tanaka who scored the controversial goal for Japan as they beat Spain at the 2022 World Cup, sending his team through to the knockout stages. The ball appeared to be out of play before Brighton and Hove Albion's Karou Mitoma played it to him.

Tanak made three further World Cup appearances this summer as Japan again reached the knockout stages.

Ethan Ampadu, Joe Rodon and Jayden Bogle all signed up until 2030 on the back of Leeds consolidating in the division last term. Over the summer they paid £30m for centre-back Tarik Muharemovic and broke their club record to pay £47m for James Trafford, in turn setting a new record for Britain's most expensive goalkeeper.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sandro Tonali has once again revealed his love for AC Milan, and spoke of the emotion of playing for his boyhood team.

Tonali played for Milan from 2020 to 2023, making 130 appearances and scoring seven goals, winning the Scudetto in 2021-22. He moved to Newcastle for €64m in what was a painful exit, given that he was being talked about as a potential future captain.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that with the Magpies, the Lodi-born midfielder played 110 games, scoring 10 goals, before moving to Tottenham Hotspur in the last summer window for €108m. There, he has linked up with Roberto De Zerbi, someone who also has Milan in his heart.

Recent findings suggest that there continues to be sporadic rumours about a return to the Rossoneri one day, but given his value it remains a pipe dream for now. Tonali was interviewed by Fútbol Emotion Italia and he recalled some significant moments that he had at Milan, with his comments relayed by Calciomercato.com.

Sources indicate that “I have two stories with AC Milan. The first is up until I was 20, when I had never fully embraced the AC Milan world. The second is from 20 onwards for the following three years,” he began.

“I was a fan for a long time. Then when the matches allowed it, maybe there was a game at San Siro when in Serie B we almost always played on Saturdays, we often went to watch. It was something passed down in the family from my father, so I’ve always had it even since I was a child.

“Then past 20 years of age it changed, because as a player you can’t maintain the same relationship with the team that you have as a fan. I did that the first year too, but I felt it too much, so after that I experienced it differently.

“But maybe it was even more beautiful because you put the fan aside and you started to realise that I suddenly found myself there, with the team of my heart and in a stadium like San Siro.

According to recent reports, “The first year wasn’t easy, I found myself struggling a bit. But it went well for me also from the point of view of playing without fans. It wasn’t nice, but for me personally as a player at that moment it was good because there was less pressure.

“But all in all it was bad because that year without fans it all seemed like friendlies, it didn’t feel like football. Milan means a lot to me.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Chelsea and England star Shaun Wright-Phillips has urged Estevao to fight tooth and nail for a starting spot at Stamford Bridge and make himself ‘hard to ignore’ under Xabi Alonso.

Estevao burst onto the scene across an eye-catching opening campaign with Chelsea having joined the club from Palmeiras in the summer of 2025, racking up eight goals and four assists for the Blues.

A serious hamstring tear brought Estevao’s debut season to a premature end, though, a devastating blow that saw him miss out on a place in Brazil’s squad at this year’s World Cup.

Just days after Estevao sustained his injury, Chelsea decided to call time on Liam Rosenior’s turbulent managerial spell – and it has proven difficult for the 19-year-old to work himself back into the side since Alonso took charge.

The teenager had been limited to only two starts in the Carabao Cup approaching late October and rumours were beginning to circulate that he had grown frustrated with his peripheral role, with Barcelona reportedly keeping tabs on the situation.

However, Joao Pedro’s absence over the last month-and-a-half has created an opportunity for Estevao in Alonso’s attack and the youngster has started two of Chelsea’s last three games.

A humbling 4-1 defeat at the hands of Leeds may not have been what Estevao had in mind for his return, though, following a substitute appearance at Sunderland, and he will no doubt be desperate to banish those memories with a strong performance versus Nottingham Forest on Friday night.

Asked if he felt that Estevao still had a big future at Chelsea under Alonso, Wright-Phillips told Metro, courtesy of kwiff: ‘It’s a hard one, because it seems like players at Chelsea outlive the managers, which is sad to say.

Industry observers note that ‘That’s where modern football is going at the minute. It seems like players are outlasting coaches.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But in general, that’s more of a tactical thing, in that Xabi plays more with wing-backs.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that ‘If you play Estevao, you want him in the front three. Chances come in random ways, so he will get his chance again, and he has to do what he did the other day.

It has been revealed that ‘When he came on, I thought he was flying: not the weekend just gone, the weekend before that [against Sunderland. He came on and played really, really well.

‘So that’s him saying, “Look, I’m good enough to stay in your squad.” If he continuously does that, it becomes hard to ignore.’.

Another player whose development has hit something of a stumbling block in recent months is Malo Gusto, who, like Estevao, has found regular game-time hard to come by this season.

Reports just last week indicated Gusto could be open to the prospect of leaving Chelsea, with Manchester United understood to be among the right-back’s admirers.

In a recent development, but when asked if it could be time to move Gusto on should a suitable offer come in for the Frenchman, Wright-Phillips replied: ‘Who do you replace him with? I think Gusto is a really fantastic player.

‘He might not be happy, which is understandable, because before Xabi came, when the other managers were there, his playing time was a lot greater, because it was either him or Reece James.

‘Reece James has had bad luck, he’s injured quite a lot, so Gusto got to play a lot. Whereas now, I think he’s better than a bit-part player, to be honest.

‘I haven’t watched him enough this season to turn around and say he should definitely be starting, but from what I saw of him last year and the type of player he is, I’d have him in my team at the drop of a hat, because I don’t think there are many right-backs out there that are gettable of that standard.’.

Chelsea splashed out in the region of £350million on fresh signings in the summer transfer window, including Morgan Rogers, who commanded a club-record fee of £117m when he joined from Aston Villa.

There were signs that the Blues were reaping the rewards of their substantial spending in a promising start to the 2026/27 campaign, with Alonso’s all-star front three firing on all cylinders.

An injury to Joao Pedro has coincided with a concerning dip in results, though, and Alonso’s men were targeted with a chorus of boos as they exited the pitch following their latest setback on Saturday.

Sources indicate that ‘I think at the very beginning he highlighted why he’s there, and at the minute it seems to have plateaued a bit. I don’t know what that’s from,’ Wright-Phillips said when asked what he had made of Alonso’s start to managerial life in the Premier League, with Chelsea languishing down in eighth.

‘Playing as many games as they have, with the internationals that have come in the way they’ve come in, it feels like the Champions League is every week; it feels like it’s the Carabao Cup or something every week at the minute.

‘It’s going to take a bit of time for the players to get used to that change, where every game is a substantial game now for everybody; literally every game comes around very quick.

‘I think those clubs will settle down and get it together because they’re lucky to have the players within that squad to do that.’.

Industry observers note that pressed on whether there were any areas of the squad in need of strengthening in January, Wright-Phillips responded: ‘I’m not sure they need midfielders. I would say if they had two, or even one, solid defenders who can teach the other young ones there, that would be more than enough.

‘Chelsea have got an amazing squad. They’re missing that rock at the back; who will fight and die for everybody, because that rubs off on the team.

‘You might not like him, but that attitude and mentality will naturally rub off on you. Someone in the Thiago Silva mould.

It has been revealed that ‘They need to learn; they’re learning from each other. They’re good players, but to get to the top, most younger players and defenders learn off somebody with a lot more experience.’.

Switching his focus to the title race, Wright-Phillips, who represented Manchester City, Chelsea and QPR during his playing days, picked out Brighton as this year’s surprise package.

And while they were beaten in stoppage time by Hull City at the weekend, the ex-England winger is confident the Seagulls remain one of Arsenal’s ‘main challengers’.

‘No disrespect to Arsenal, but the best club for me in the Premier League this season, to watch and for output, is Brighton,’ Wright-Phillips – a Premier League winner with Chelsea in 2006 – explained.

‘Brighton are probably playing the best, but they’re not at the top of the league.

Industry observers note that ‘It can change and go a different way. I don’t think Arsenal are playing that well, and I don’t think City have played that well, but they’re the two teams that know how to get results when they aren’t playing to the level they know their maximum is.

‘Unfortunately for City, that hasn’t happened in the last four games, which is something they have to deal with and turn around.

‘The Christmas period is the right time to possibly do it, because all the games come quick and fast and the league table can change a dozen times in that time.

‘The main challengers to Arsenal would be Brighton and Manchester City as it stands. They’re the ones with the points on the board.

‘Until people start putting the points on the board, which is turning around, you’re seeing Liverpool sneak back up the table.

‘There will be other challenges as well, but leading into this Christmas period, I would say Arsenal’s challenger right now is Brighton and Manchester City.

It has been revealed that ‘Brighton, I think, are the only team to beat both of those two teams and do it nicely as well. It wasn’t a smash and grab.’.

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 08:12, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 08:15.

Manchester United will be aiming to win for just the second time in the Premier League this season when they welcome Brentford to Old Trafford.

The Red Devils, who are 19th in the Premier League table, will enter the match off the back of a 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Premier League contest will kick off at 3pm UK time on Saturday.

The match will take place at Man United's home stadium, Old Trafford.

Man United recorded a 2-1 win over Brentford in the corresponding match during the 2025-26 campaign, and the Bees have never triumphed at Old Trafford in the Premier League.

The Premier League contest at Old Trafford will not be available to watch in the UK due to the 3pm blackout rule.

Sky Sports will show highlights on their social media and YouTube channels, as well as on their dedicated app on Saturday evening.

UK viewers can also watch the highlights of the game on Match of the Day, which will start at 10:30pm on BBC One and run until 11:30pm.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a disastrous Premier League campaign to date for the 20-time English champions, who were thumped 4-0 at Liverpool last weekend.

The Red Devils are in a genuine relegation battle at this moment in time, and this is shaping up to be another incredibly difficult match against a talented Brentford outfit.

Man United were in Champions League action on Wednesday, and Mauricio Pochettino's side did put in a much-improved performance in a 2-2 draw with Sporting.

The Bees will enter the match off the back of a 4-0 win over Everton, and they right now sit sixth in the table, only one point off fifth-placed Bournemouth.

Brentford are bidding to win at Old Trafford for the first time in the Premier League, but they have triumphed in two of the last three matches between the two sides.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Former England footballer Raheem Sterling, 31, has been handed a suspended prison sentence today.

He was sentenced to 12 months in prison, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court after dangerously driving his Lamborghini and possessing nitrous oxide canisters.

Sterling was also ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months.

He had been seen by other motorists inhaling from a balloon while driving his black sports car, swerving in and out of lanes – with one driver ‘shocked’ by what he saw, a court previously heard.

Sterling arrived at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court this morning, wearing a black top and dark trousers.

He has been on unconditional bail and subject to an interim driving ban since he admitted offences in September.

The former Manchester City player had pleaded guilty at the Hampshire court to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before he crashed on the morning of May 28.

Sterling also admitted possession of six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.

Police body-worn footage of the footballer’s arrest at 9.15am demonstrates him in the crashed car with two canisters on his lap as the officer tells him: ‘You can put that down mate.’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The court previously heard witness Christopher Jennings on the M25 called 999 at 7.49am after he was driving in parallel to Sterling’s car and ‘he was shocked by what he saw’.

Sterling scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate’s side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the final of Euro 2020.

He came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut.

Sterling, who was born in Kingston, Jamaica, moved to Manchester City in 2015 and won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019.

He left for Chelsea in 2022 but, after falling out of favour, spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal.

After leaving Stamford Bridge, Sterling joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of the season.

He is presently without a club.

Sterling was made an MBE in the 2021 Queen’s Birthday Honours for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out against racism on and off the pitch for several years.

It came amid controversy over England fans booing players taking the knee at matches as a gesture against intolerance.

Tel, meanwhile, is expected to be out for up to three weeks after sustaining an ankle injury against Leeds before the international week.

With Mudryk and Tel absent against Ipswich, De Zerbi selected Savio in a matchday squad for the first time since October 10 after he suffered a muscular injury in training.

#164962. The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1172 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships.
  • Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.
  • The dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships. But there's at least one of these muses who was freed from toxic romantic entanglement: a cute dachshund called Lump.

Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.

The dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967. According to Duncan, upon their first encounter, Lump jumped right onto Picasso's lap. He apparently "decided" to stay with the painter, and they lived together for six years.

The story does not reveal how Lump's decision was communicated, but that immediate special bound was immortalized through art: Picasso painted the dachshund's portrait directly onto a ceramic dinner plate that day, and Duncan did a series of photos documenting them together while the work was created.

Recent findings suggest that the plate and the photos are on show at the new exhibition "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash" held at the Kunsthalle Bremen until March 28, 2027.

Lump also appears in many of Picasso's series of paintings reinterpreting Diego Velazquez's masterwork "Las Meninas," in which the original work's large mastiff was replaced with Picasso's adoptive pet.

With their long ears and extreme length compared to their short legs, dachshunds have a silhouette that's instantly recognizable: "It's really a dog with an iconic shape, and that makes them interesting for many things" — from art to advertisement, indicates exhibition curator and art historian Annett Reckert.

It has been revealed that alongside Picasso, a surprising number of notable artists, including Andy Warhol, Otto Dix, David Hockney, Max Liebermann and Rosemarie Trockel, have paid tribute to the dachshund. "It's striking how often the dachshund has served as a muse, model and studio accomplice for them," Reckert tells DW.

Combined with this prolific artistic career, the dachshund can equally be explored from a historical perspective, since "there's also the fact that we associate them with something German," the curator adds.

Sources indicate that bred to track and chase badgers, foxes, rabbits and other burrowing animals, the dachshund originated in Germany over 300 years ago. Breed standards were established in 1879, and the German Teckel Club (DTK) — one of the oldest dog breeding organizations in Germany — was founded in 1888.

The name combines the German words "Dachs" (badger) and "Hund" (dog), literally translating to "badger dog." But Germans more commonly call them Dackel or Teckel.

Because of their long, narrow build, dachshunds are also colloquially known in English-speaking countries as wiener dogs or sausage dogs.

Beyond their role as hunting dogs, dachshunds have a surprisingly rich place in German cultural history, from bourgeois stereotype to Olympic icon.

Germany's last emperor, Kaiser Wilhelm II, was an avid dachshund enthusiast and owned several of them.

Industry observers note that two of his dogs, Wadl and Hexlsome, made history by causing a minor diplomatic incident during a visit to the estate of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, Konopiste Castle, in 1908. The dachshunds reportedly killed one of the archduke's prized golden pheasants. The attack was widely commented on in aristocratic circles, and Kaiser Wilhelm II was forced to issue a formal apology.

The pheasant incident was obviously not as consequential as another event involving Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne: his assassination in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, which became the primary catalyst of World War I.

According to recent reports, still, the dachshund remained present throughout this global conflict. In propaganda maps and political cartoons, Germany was represented as a dachshund, the British as a bulldog and the French, a poodle.

The popularity of the dachshund in the United States plummeted during the World War I because of this association; those who owned one called their dogs "liberty hounds" instead of using the German word.

During World War II, dachshunds were used for military tasks such as mine detection.

However, their missions weren't as outlandish as the stories published by the UK's tabloid press relatively recently, which claimed that the Nazis aimed to build armies of talking dachshunds. The rumors followed the publication of a non-fiction book on dogs published in 2011, "Amazing Dogs: A Cabinet of Canine Curiosities," which outlined Nazi research into dogs' — including dachshunds' — intelligence and personalities.

The dachshund definitely didn't fit into the Nazis' aesthetics: "They were used in the war, too, but not in the same way as other dogs. After all, they weren't the kind of dog a Nazi would have wanted to be seen with for the sake of appearances," notes Reckert. "Take Hitler, for instance: He famously made public appearances with his German Shepherd, Blondie. They would rather be seen with a Doberman or dogs that looked significant and dangerous.".

The endearing potential of the dachshund is actually one of the ideas that guided Reckert in her curation of the exhibition. They "simply give the impression that they have a sense of humor," the art historian states. "That's an attribution, of course. But they really do spread good cheer and have a truly likable character.".

In the 1970s, this slightly absurd and cheerful domestic companion inspired a figure embodying a new image for West Germany: the official mascot for the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich, Waldi.

A stark contrast to the heavy symbols that represented Germany during the Third Reich — the eagle, Germania, forests, Wagner and Prussian discipline — the mascot created by renowned graphic designer Otl Aicher and his intern, Elena Schwaiger, was as iconic as the shape of the dachshund.

In a recent development, the designer was vehemently against including brown or any of Germany's national colors — red, black and gold — in the brand identity. Instead, he went for delicate pastel shades: "The approach to color was truly visionary," notes Reckert. "Their intention was something we are still working on today — something we still haven't completely achieved: an open, cheerful, democratic and colorful Germany.".

Still today, right-wing extremist groups attempt to co-opt the dachshund as a subtle nationalist fashion symbol that appears on ties or socks, inspired by accessories worn by Alexander Gauland. On the other hand, "Dachshunds Against the Right" has also emerged as a counter-protest movement.

Industry observers note that but altogether, Reckert has focused on the dachshund as a symbol of friendliness and joy while conceiving "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash." The exhibition includes halls that are open to small dogs and even features artworks and performances specifically designed for them.

According to recent reports, the feedback Reckert's been getting in the run-up to the show also aligns with this cheerful image. She notes that hardly a day goes by without something arriving in the mail related to the dachshund — whether pictures, artworks or information about dachshund-related events.

"It's really crazy," she says, showing examples of the stuff she's received. "I've never had an exhibition that was greeted ahead of its opening in such a friendly, diverse way. It's almost a bit uncanny, really.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 12:29 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 12:33 EST, 25 November 2026.

Even for aficionados of the continental game, the draw for the Europa League this year was likely to cause a degree of puzzlement.

In a recent development, while not the only outfit to be making its debut in one of UEFA’s competitions, the name of S.C.U. Torreense rang precious few bells among supporters of clubs with a vested interest in how the cards might fall. And little wonder.

The Portuguese side are plankton in football’s great ocean. Not only have they never played on this stage before, they haven’t even come close to it.

An extraordinary triumph in the Portuguese Cup final – the Taca de Portugal – against Sporting Lisbon in May was their ticket to this journey. In all likelihood, this European adventure will be their first and their last.

Sources indicate that it is, of course, not the done thing for anyone connected with any particular club to express a preference as to who they might be drawn against. But representatives of any one of the 35 other sides present at the Grimaldi Forum in Monaco in late August who claimed they weren’t privately hoping for a match against the men from the small city of Torres Vedras were lying.

Industry observers note that never mind Benfica, Porto and Sporting Lisbon, the traditional footballing powerhouses of that nation. In terms of support, stature and history, this outfit are a world removed from the likes of Braga and Vitoria Guimaraes, the perennial challengers to the massive three.

Torreense players celebrate their victory over Armenian side Ararat in their last European tie.

Torreense’s place in the food chain is underscored by the fact that they can’t even play European matches in their 2,400-capacity Estadio Manuel Marques home because it doesn’t match UEFA criteria.

For the purposes of the Europa League, their fans, who primarily hail from a place which sits 25 miles north of Lisbon, will have to travel to Leiria, which is 60 miles north of their home.

Those looking to pick up a late ticket for the visit of Celtic should have no concerns. Built for Euro 2004, the Estadio Municipal de Leiria holds 23,888 spectators. Torreense, who were a tier three side as recently as 2022, draw an average crowd of around 1,300.

The fact is that it’s not only a second division Portuguese side which Martin O’Neill’s men will face on matchday five. It’s a struggling one.

Recent findings suggest that after ten matches in Liga Portugal 2, Joao Nuno’s men lie 13th of 18, 31st place overall in Portugal. They’ve won just twice this season, against Amarante and Benfica B, and have already had their cup defence ended by Benfica’s massive boys.

Nuno was only appointed at the end of October after Luis Tralhao, who lifted the only major honour in the club’s history, was fired after a dismal start.

Portuguese coach Joao Nuno only took charge at the struggling second-tier side this season.

Yet the concern for O’Neill and his players is that the Torreense which routinely fails to impress in its domestic division bears little resemblance to the one which has so far pitched up on its maiden European adventure.

In one of the most eye-catching results of the opening night, the Portuguese minnows travelled to Norway and defeated Lillestrom, a respected name throughout Europe, 2-1.

Sunderland were the first visitors to Leiria in October. What a game Torreense gave the Premier League side, leading by a goal only to narrowly lose the match late on.

While a 4-1 loss to Celtic’s old foes Ferencvaros in Budapest was something of a reality check, Nuno’s players fought back from a goal down to beat Ararat-Armenia in injury time last time out at their adopted home.

So, despite being wretched in their own league, they have six points in the Europa League and presently sit in 19th place, above the likes of Real Sociedad, AC Milan and Marseille.

According to recent reports, with nine points possibly being enough to squeeze through to the play-off round, a famous win against Celtic could do the trick with three games to spare. With around £400,000 earned in prize money for any victory, you’d better believe they’ll be up for this.

Having just about lived to tell the tale last month, Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris gave Celtic a warning about what lies in store on Thursday.

Despite their lowly status, Torreense are above AC Milan, Celtic and Marseille in the table.

Industry observers note that ‘It’s a good team they know how to manage this kind of game,’ mentioned the Frenchman. ‘They’re well organised and hard to break down with this deep block. They try to seize every opportunity.’.

A limited side which sits in and plays with caution? Those Celtic supporters who had the misfortune to watch their favourites fail to break down an atrocious Kairat Almaty outfit across 210 minutes little over a year ago will be rightly concerned.

While the Parkhead men’s poor record on the road across many years includes some thumpings at the hands of super clubs including Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain, there have been enough stumbles against lesser sides to ensure nothing can be taken for granted.

Industry observers note that O’Neill will point to the displays in last season’s victories away to Feyenoord and Stuttgart as examples of what he’s looking for. While not on his watch, the catastrophe away to Kairat remains a useful illustration of what may happen if the players aren’t at it.

With an early goal likely to kick the legs from under Torreense, Celtic cannot allow them to feel comfortable in their shape.

In order to disrupt the Portuguese, it will be a night for the visitors to play with speed and imagination. To get in behind their defence, O’Neill’s wingers need to shine.

Sunderland required a late goal from Noah Sadiki to emerge with a victory on their trip to Leiria.

This will have informed the veteran’s thinking as he sought to draft in a replacement for the injured Mika Baur.

Recent findings suggest that while bringing in Joel van den Berg would have made sense from a positional point of view, Jota has started to show signs that he’s moving through the levels after a year-and-a-half out injured. A goal or an assist on his return to his homeland would allow the former Benfica man to underscore that point.

A constant threat against St Mirren, Yang Hyun-jun should start on the right flank ahead of Haissem Hassan. Together with Seb Tounekti, the Egyptian increasingly feels like a peripheral player.

Even if Benjamin Nygren is available again after a heel injury, O’Neill will be loath to drop Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain or Luke McCowan after both indicated up well when played alongside Callum McGregor in the weekend win.

The matter of Kasper Hogh’s 16-game goal drought will only become pertinent if the free-scoring Camilo Duran can first help to put the game to bed.

Fit-again winger Jota could feature for Celtic on his return to Portuguese soil.

Celtic badly need this to be a rare straightforward evening on the road in Europe. Goodness knows, they’ve had precious few of those in recent times.

A win to go with the one they claimed last time out against Besiktas would leave them in a decent position in the competition, with a further four points from their remaining matches with Omonia, Marseille and Union Saint-Gilloise then assuring them of progression.

Industry observers note that anything other than that outcome tonight doesn’t bear thinking about. Almost 60 years on from Jock Stein’s side becoming sporting immortals by defeating Inter Milan in Lisbon, their successors must tick a box and ensure tiny Torreense’s reputation in the game remains as lowly as it has ever been.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that the best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman noted. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

In a recent development, “We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”.

In a recent development, avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

Sources indicate that “When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman mentioned. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

In a recent development, “That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

Industry observers note that all eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”.

Recent findings suggest that toone rapidly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”.

Recent findings suggest that that opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven massive-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

Luka Vuskovic has revealed he chose to leave Tottenham for career stability, admitting that not a single Spurs manager spoke to him during the three years he was on the club’s books.

Vuskovic joined Spurs in 2023 in a £12million deal from Croatian side Hajduk Split before being sent on loan to Radomiak Radom in Poland, Westerlo in Belgium and German outfit Hamburg.

During that time, Vuskovic developed a reputation as one of Europe’s brightest young defenders and was named in last year’s Bundesliga team of the season.

The 19-year-old, who was called up to Croatia’s World Cup squad over the summer, returned to Spurs at the end of last season but found his path to the first team blocked as Roberto De Zerbi’s side moved swiftly to sign centre-backs Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi.

Spurs wanted Vuskovic to go out on loan again, with De Zerbi unable to offer him a place in the starting lineup, but the youngster was not keen on another season of upheaval and made it clear he wanted a permanent home.

With Spurs unwilling to offer Vuskovic assurances over his playing time, they agreed a £52m deal with Brighton.

The move has paid off handsomely for Vuskovic, who has been a key part of Brighton’s stellar start to the season, with the Seagulls second in the Premier League, and he says he had decided his future early this summer.

Industry observers note that “That (a loan) was their idea, but it was never an option from my side,” Vuskovic said in an interview with the Times. “Because already I have been on three loans and for me, my family, my girlfriend, it’s too much to move, with all the languages, and it gets too much for the person, you know?

“Before they signed everybody, they mentioned they don’t see me at the moment as a starting player.

It has been revealed that “Tottenham mentioned they don’t want me at the minute, so I said, ‘OK, I have no problem with that, you gave me a loan already when I was 16, I just want to play somewhere where the club wants me. You can earn from me, so I think it’s fair for both of us.’ ”.

You want to be somewhere where you are stable, where you can spend a few years, where you can develop more.

Luka Vuskovic on picking Brighton.

Vuskovic’s performances have prompted transfer links with the likes of Liverpool and fellow European giants, but the youngster is happy at Brighton for now.

Sources indicate that he continued: “You want to be somewhere where you are stable, where you can spend a few years, where you can develop more, where you can meet friends, people, connect with somebody. We wanted that, and in the end we got it.”.

Vuskovic never made a senior competitive appearance for Spurs and was out on loan as the club went from Europa League winners to relegation candidates in the space of 12 chaotic months.

During that period, Spurs went through four different managers, with Ange Postecoglu, Thomas Frank, Igor Tudor and De Zerbi all in the hot seat while Vuskovic watched from afar at Hamburg.

Despite being on the books at Spurs, Vuskovic’s future at the club was always up in the air, and he admits he never once got a call from any of the club’s managers to check on him when he was out on loan.

“I never spoke with any Tottenham coach. They never called me,” Vuskovic continued.

Recent findings suggest that “I had one guy from Tottenham, Andy [Scoulding, Tottenham’s performance manager], he spent a lot of time calling me, asking if I need help, and also some physios if I ever needed anything, nutritionists also. But never from the coaches.”.

Manchester United have been urged to avoid pursuing a move for wantaway Chelsea full-back Malo Gusto in the January transfer window.

United made a disappointing start to life under their newly introduced head coach Mauricio Pochettino, shipping four goals as they fell to a dispiriting defeat against Liverpool.

The scale of the task at hand will now be all the more apparent to Pochettino, with his side now winless in nine Premier League matches and just one point off bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace.

The upcoming January transfer window may provide a precious opportunity for United to add some much-needed defensive depth to their squad.

Calvin Bassey is among the rumoured targets at centre-back, while Chelsea full-back Gusto has also been linked with a move to Old Trafford.

But Mikael Silvestre urged his former club against a move for Gusto, insisting Pochettino instead needs players who are in form and can hit the ground running straight away.

‘Manchester United should definitely not be looking to sign Malo Gusto,’ Silvestre told BestBettingBonuses.

‘He is not the right player for this current United defence, especially with the confidence so low.

Industry observers note that ‘Gusto is in a difficult place mentally. He had a torrid game with France during the last international window, and he’s not in the Chelsea starting eleven.

‘Right now, United need players who are confident in their mind; players who know themselves and are sure about their capabilities.

In a recent development, ‘I think it would be crazy to bring in a player like Gusto into a United defence that is so unsettled. You don’t want to add more problems.

‘We have enough problems on our own right now. He would also cost a lot of money, and you could argue that it would be better spent on other players.’.

Silvestre was similarly uninspired by United’s rumoured pursuit of Bassey, adding: ‘I have to be honest, Bassey is not a player that excites me or who I think would upgrade the United defence.

‘Manchester United need to sign players that are going to raise the level, and those players wouldn’t do that.’.

Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 80 min read (16062 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~80 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Heterochromatin typically represses genes1,2, yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation3,4,5,6,7.
  • In a recent development, histone H3 lysine 9 (H3 K9) trimethylation, a canonical post-translational modification of constitutive heterochromatin, is known to spread over large genomic territories and repress gene expression9.
  • According to recent reports, the vertebrate clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus provides a striking example of a large gene family whose expression has been proposed to require escape from a heterochromatic environment10,11,12,13.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Heterochromatin typically represses genes1,2, yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation3,4,5,6,7. How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent8. In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self–non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly8. By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer–promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments.

In a recent development, histone H3 lysine 9 (H3 K9) trimethylation, a canonical post-translational modification of constitutive heterochromatin, is known to spread over large genomic territories and repress gene expression9. These defining properties of heterochromatin were recognized in classic position–effect variegation studies in Drosophila during the 1930s, in which euchromatic genes placed near domains with trimethylated H3 K9 (H3K9me3) became transcriptionally silenced1,2. However, subsequent discovery of genes whose expression depends on their residence within heterochromatin revealed that this conflict is not absolute. For example, expression of the light (lt) and rolled (rl) genes in flies requires their position within pericentromeric heterochromatin3,4,5. In mice and humans, proper expression of olfactory receptor (OR) and KRAB domain-containing zinc-finger protein (KZFP) genes also depends on H3K9me3 heterochromatin6,7. These ‘escapee’ genes suggest the existence of specialized regulatory strategies that allow transcription to occur within, or despite, heterochromatin, raising fundamental questions about when heterochromatin facilitates versus restrains gene expression.

According to recent reports, the vertebrate clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus provides a striking example of a large gene family whose expression has been proposed to require escape from a heterochromatic environment10,11,12,13. Pcdh genes are expressed predominantly in neurons, where they govern neuronal self–non-self discrimination and circuit formation8. In individual neurons, only a small subset of Pcdh genes are expressed, whereas most remain silent8. Because selection of Pcdh genes is random and combinatorial14,15,16,17, this process generates extraordinary cell surface protein isoform diversity that marks each neuron with a unique identity, or ‘barcode’. Neurites presenting the same Pcdh barcode recognize and avoid one another, thereby preventing self-adhesion, whereas neurites presenting distinct Pcdh barcodes do not self-recognize and can interact18,19,20. Consistent with their critical role in neural circuit assembly, genetic variants in Pcdh genes are associated with neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders, including autism spectrum disorder21,22 and schizophrenia23.

Sources indicate that in mice, there are 58 Pcdh genes distributed across three tandemly arranged clusters—α (Pcdha), β (Pcdhb) and γ (Pcdhg)—spanning roughly 1 megabase of DNA on chromosome 18 (ref. 24) (Fig. 1a). Pcdha genes are regulated by the HS5-1 enhancer located downstream of the Pcdha cluster, whereas Pcdhb and Pcdhg genes are regulated by the HS18-22 and HS16-17 enhancers, respectively, located downstream of the Pcdhg cluster25 (Fig. 1a). The Pcdha and Pcdhg genes are further subdivided into ‘alternate’ and ‘c-type’ isoforms24 (Fig. 1a). Pcdh genes and their promoters are marked by H3 K9 trimethylation and CpG DNA methylation (5mC)10,13,26. Stochastic Pcdh gene choice requires promoter DNA demethylation driven by cohesin-mediated enhancer–promoter interactions, with promoter demethylation leading to CTCF binding and sustained transcription of the respective Pcdh gene10,13,15,27,28. Although these findings have identified how Pcdh promoters escape DNA methylation, they do not address how euchromatic Pcdh enhancers navigate H3K9me3 heterochromatin to activate silent Pcdh promoters. Several questions remain unanswered. Specifically, do stochastic enhancer–promoter interactions occur within heterochromatin? Is Pcdh transcription carried out within a heterochromatic environment otherwise programmed to suppress gene activity, or must Pcdh loci escape this environment to transcribe? And, does heterochromatin contribute to the stochasticity of Pcdh promoter choice?

To answer these questions, we sought a single-molecule view of Pcdh locus architecture during development that included the positioning of active and inactive promoters. Until now, most insights into this relationship have come from bulk genomic analyses. At a locus where only a few genes are active while most remain silent, bulk measurements mainly reflect the non-chosen genes, effectively averaging out the features of the chosen ones. To circumvent this limitation, we used optical reconstruction of chromatin architecture (ORCA), a single-molecule chromatin tracing assay29, in olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs) of the mouse olfactory epithelium (OE). We selected OSNs for three reasons. First, they undergo multiple stages of development and constantly regenerate, such that each stage is present within the OE simultaneously. Second, Pcdh gene expression is developmentally regulated during OSN maturation15,20, with approximately one gene per cluster expressed from each allele in mature OSNs (mOSNs) (Fig. 1b and Extended Data Fig. 1a–c). Third, stochastic expression of Pcdh genes has a critical role in OSN axon wiring and odour map formation20,30,31.

Recent findings suggest that we designed ORCA probes that tile the Pcdh locus in 90 10-kilobase bins, omitting repetitive and GC-poor regions (Fig. 1a). ORCA probes were validated in OE sections from mice in which mOSNs were genetically labelled (Extended Data Fig. 2a). We visualized ORCA data as contact frequency matrices, which depict the frequency that each pair of locus positions (bins along the Pcdh locus) falls within a specified three-dimensional (3D) distance across all imaged traces. We set this threshold near the average distance between adjacent locus positions in an experiment. The contact frequency map obtained from ORCA correlated strongly with chromosome conformation capture Hi-C data of the same genomic bins from sorted mOSNs (Extended Data Fig. 2b,c, Pearson’s r = 0.87), and the correlation remained high across a sweep of ORCA contact thresholds (Extended Data Fig. 2d). ORCA data from whole OE tissue also remained consistent across separate experiments (Extended Data Fig. 2e,f, Pearson’s r = 0.98) and indicated good detection efficiency across locus positions (Extended Data Fig. 2g). These results demonstrate that ORCA faithfully captures Pcdh locus architecture.

According to recent reports, to study how Pcdh locus architecture changes during Pcdh gene activation and neuronal maturation, we combined ORCA imaging of Pcdh DNA with RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) labelling of the five major OSN developmental cell stages: horizontal basal cells (HBCs), globose basal cells (GBCs), immediate neuronal precursors (INPs), immature OSNs (iOSNs) and mOSNs (Fig. 1c). This lineage spawns from the mitotic HBC population located near the basal surface of the OE. As OSNs progress along their developmental axis, these cells migrate towards the apical surface of the OE (Fig. 1c). RNA labelling of marker genes for each stage reflected this basal-to-apical migration (Fig. 1d). We also stained samples with fluorescently tagged wheat germ agglutinin (WGA), a lectin that binds cell membranes, to obtain 3D segmentations of cells in the OE (Extended Data Fig. 3a). We mapped both RNA and Pcdh DNA puncta to these segmentations, then classified ORCA traces (that is, individual DNA paths) into different developmental stages on the basis of the RNA signal of the cells in which they resided (Extended Data Fig. 3b,c).

The contact frequency maps for each stage of OSN development illustrated two trends. First, stripes denoting contacts between Pcdh enhancers and their target promoters became more prominent as cells matured (Fig. 1e and Extended Data Fig. 1d–f). Second, contacts between locus positions containing Pcdhb genes and the alternate genes from the Pcdha and Pcdhg clusters, as well as the 60-kilobase stretch upstream of the Pcdha genes, increased (Fig. 1e,f). Subtracting the contact frequency map of each developmental stage from the mOSN map emphasized that these inter-cluster contacts constituted the most pronounced changes in locus architecture over development (Fig. 1e).

Industry observers note that the formation of these inter-cluster contact domains was reminiscent of the checkerboard pattern created by compartmentalization of active and repressed chromatin domains seen on Hi-C maps32. Given that this compartmentalization is mainly driven by homotypic interactions between heterochromatic regions of the genome, we hypothesized that the locus regions engaging in these contacts would have histone marks characteristic of heterochromatin. To investigate this possibility, we performed quantitative native chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (nChIP–seq) for H3K9me3 in FACS-isolated HBCs and mOSNs. In HBCs, the Pcdh locus was lightly coated in H3K9me3, with H3K9me3 levels increasing roughly threefold in mOSNs (Fig. 1g,h). Furthermore, in mOSNs, two major stretches of enriched H3K9me3 emerged separated by regions devoid of H3K9me3 between and beyond them (Fig. 1g). Specifically, the DNA regions of the Pcdh locus that engaged in inter-cluster contacts over OSN development became heavily coated with H3K9me3, whereas regions of the locus containing Pcdh c-type genes and enhancers remained free of H3K9me3 (Fig. 1e,g). We hereafter refer to the H3K9me3-marked chromatin regions engaging in inter-cluster contacts as the ‘heterochromatin domain’ of the Pcdh locus. This definition indicates the spatial arrangement of the regions within the Pcdh locus that are marked by H3K9me3 in OSNs. We refer to the regions of the locus not marked by H3K9me3 containing Pcdh c-type genes and enhancers as euchromatin.

Sources indicate that to understand the positioning of the heterochromatin domain within the architecture of the Pcdh locus, we calculated the distance of each locus position to the geometric centre of its respective trace and examined the median over all traces across each stage of development. All locus positions moved closer to the geometric centre as cells matured, indicating a general compaction of the locus (Fig. 1i). Layered on top of this trend, locus positions belonging to the heterochromatin domain moved closest to the centre (Fig. 1i, boxed regions), whereas euchromatic regions remained further in the periphery. To better quantify the degree of compaction of the heterochromatin domain, we measured its radius of gyration (Rg), a metric commonly used to describe the volume of a polymer, and found that Rg decreases as neurons mature (Fig. 1j). Surprisingly, as compaction increases, so does the number of genes expressed per cell from within the domain (Fig. 1j). We further visualized these changes in locus architecture by plotting individual traces coloured by regions that become heterochromatic or euchromatic over development and by examining single-molecule distance maps (Fig. 1k and Extended Data Fig. 4). Despite heterogeneity across traces, the formation of the domain was evident: in HBCs, both regions tended to occupy large and intermixed volumes, whereas in mOSNs, the regions segregated, with heterochromatin forming a dense, more centrally located domain and euchromatin occupying more open volumes in the periphery (Fig. 1k and Extended Data Fig. 4).

In a recent development, overall, these results indicate that in neural stem cells, the Pcdh locus is lightly coated with H3K9me3 heterochromatin, yet open and intermixed, with a compact heterochromatin domain forming in its centre as cells mature into post-mitotic neurons (Fig. 1l). Counterintuitively, the formation of this compact structure coincides with activation of Pcdh genes (Fig. 1j).

Sources indicate that these results could be explained by the presence of two distinct subpopulations—actively transcribing loci that transiently lose heterochromatin and silent loci that do not. Alternatively, actively transcribing loci could retain heterochromatin and their compacted architecture. Because our bulk measurements of H3K9me3 by nChIP–seq could not distinguish between these two possibilities, we turned to stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (STORM) to measure H3K9me3 in single cells. We combined STORM for H3K9me3 with RNA FISH labelling of Pcdh isoforms and OSN cell types, as well as ORCA imaging of DNA, to test for colocalization of heterochromatin with transcribing Pcdh alleles (Fig. 2a). We used RNA probes against 11 Pcdh isoforms and confirmed their specificity for their target isoforms in vitro (Extended Data Fig. 5a,b).

Overlaying Pcdh RNA staining on Pcdh DNA loci labelled by ORCA revealed DNA traces that colocalized with RNA puncta (Extended Data Fig. 6a). By measuring distances between Pcdh loci and Pcdh RNA puncta, we identified a data-driven distance threshold below which RNA transcripts could be classified as nascent (Extended Data Fig. 6b,c). RNA puncta within this threshold were brighter than those beyond it, consistent with nascent transcriptional bursting33 (Extended Data Fig. 6d).

According to recent reports, we then examined the spatial relationship between transcribing Pcdh DNA loci and H3K9me3 STORM signal in mOSNs. Remarkably, we observed many examples of nascent transcription occurring at Pcdh loci that colocalized with H3K9me3 STORM (Fig. 2b and Extended Data Fig. 7a). Plotting the ORCA traces of these loci alongside H3K9me3 STORM localizations revealed transcribing promoters spatially residing within heterochromatin (Fig. 2b and Extended Data Fig. 7a).

Industry observers note that to assess whether STORM captured a nuclear enrichment of H3K9me3 over the Pcdh locus, we quantified the number of H3K9me3 localizations surrounding Pcdh loci relative to randomized positions within the same nuclei. The median number of H3K9me3 localizations detected around Pcdh DNA loci exceeded that of randomized positions in 999 of 1,000 simulations (empirical P = 0.002) (Fig. 2c). We performed the same analyses on Tex15 loci, which are not marked by H3K9me3 as assayed by bulk nChIP–seq (Extended Data Fig. 7b–d). We used Tex15 nascent RNA transcripts as proxies for Tex15 DNA positions (Extended Data Fig. 7c,d). In contrast to Pcdh loci, Tex15 loci did not show an enrichment for H3K9me3 (empirical P = 0.292) (Extended Data Fig. 7d). Furthermore, we observed more Tex15 loci lacking any H3K9me3 signal compared with Pcdh loci (Extended Data Fig. 7e).

We next asked whether Pcdh transcription was associated with reduced local H3K9me3 signal and domain compaction by first dividing loci into those with or without detectable nascent transcription, the latter of which we hereafter refer to as non-transcribing. We then measured the number of H3K9me3 STORM localizations around these loci and the Rg of their heterochromatin domains by ORCA. Surprisingly, transcribing Pcdh loci had slightly higher H3K9me3 STORM signal and slightly more compact heterochromatin domains relative to non-transcribing loci (Fig. 2d,e). Furthermore, transcription of individual Pcdh genes was associated neither with a change in H3K9me3 STORM signal around transcribing promoters, at the resolution of our assay, nor with a change in heterochromatin domain compaction (Fig. 2f,g).

Overall, these analyses indicate that transcription of Pcdh loci can occur in H3K9me3-rich nuclear territories and does not disrupt the heterochromatin domain of the locus.

It has been revealed that these data prompted us to further evaluate features of a transcribing Pcdh locus. To do that, we expanded the design of our RNA probes to a total of 31 Pcdh genes that showed appreciable staining and specificity (Extended Data Fig. 5a,b). We noted that nascently transcribing RNA puncta often colocalized with other Pcdh RNAs of the same cluster (Fig. 3a), and more nascent puncta were detected for progressively downstream isoforms at the Pcdha and Pcdhg, but not Pcdhb, clusters (Fig. 3b). Meanwhile, mature transcript levels measured by bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) remained relatively flat across all clusters (Fig. 3b). We reasoned that these results could reflect nascent transcription of Pcdha and Pcdhg genes that reads through downstream isoforms (Fig. 3c). Yet, the number of nascent Pcdh RNAs detected at a locus was not associated with changes in heterochromatin domain Rg (Fig. 3d), indicating that this putative transcriptional readthrough occurs without domain decompaction.

Industry observers note that to identify features of locus architecture associated with transcription, we subtracted the contact frequency maps of non-transcribing loci from the maps of transcribing loci in mOSNs. This revealed an enrichment of enhancer–promoter contacts in transcribing loci (Fig. 3e–g), which was further supported by an increase in transcription probability as a function of enhancer–promoter proximity (Extended Data Fig. 8). For Pcdha and Pcdhg genes, these enhancer–promoter contact enrichments included promoters upstream of the transcribing isoform, and the magnitude of enrichment experienced by each promoter diminished when filtering on transcription of progressively downstream isoforms (Fig. 3e,g). By contrast, Pcdhb promoters had more local enhancer-contact enrichments upon transcription (Fig. 3f).

It has been revealed that together, these data indicate that at the Pcdha and Pcdhg clusters, transcription of chosen promoters reads through downstream genes. This pattern is consistent with splicing of Pcdha and Pcdhg variable exons to three small constant exons located 3′ of these clusters34, and was not observed at the Pcdhb cluster, which lacks constant exons. Furthermore, these data indicate that Pcdh gene choice is driven by highly specific enhancer–promoter interactions across this multi-gene, multi-enhancer locus.

Sources indicate that we next asked where Pcdh transcription and enhancer–promoter interactions occur within the spatial architecture of the locus (Fig. 1l) and, in particular, whether transcribing promoters remain within or exit the heterochromatin domain. To assess the positioning of transcribing promoters, we measured the distances between promoters and heterochromatic locus positions in the presence and absence of transcription in mOSNs (Fig. 4a). These distances did not change during transcription (Fig. 4a). On the other hand, distances between promoters and euchromatic locus positions decreased during transcription (Fig. 4a). This effect seemed driven by decreased distances between promoters and enhancers upon transcription (Fig. 4b). These results indicate that enhancer–promoter contacts associated with transcription bring euchromatic locus positions closer to the heterochromatin domain, but neither these contacts nor transcription itself cause transcribing promoters to exit the domain. Plotting transcription probability as a function of a promoter’s distance to the heterochromatin centre supported this conclusion, as promoters were most likely to be transcribing at distances within the median Rg of the heterochromatin domain (Fig. 4c).
